endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Relevant testing may include differential diagnosis generation assessed for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses, multi-turn simulated encounters scored for the quality and sequencing of follow-up questions, and scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.

endorsements.title: Toward Clinical Generative AI: Conceptual Framework
endorsements.quote: The false myth paradigm tests the AI’s ability to reject outdated concepts or information and content not substantiated by scientific evidence, whereas the challenging question paradigm assesses how AI handles nuanced medical issues.

endorsements.title: The Clinicians' Guide to Large Language Models: A General Perspective With a Focus on Hallucinations
endorsements.quote: Furthermore, the scientific adequacy of the LLM’s responses should be assessed with regard to current standards of care and up-to-date guidelines.

endorsements.title: [Can large language models answer clinical questions?]
endorsements.quote: La valutazione dell’accuratezza di questi modelli rispetto a tali linee guida è quindi cruciale per garantire che possano essere utilizzati in modo sicuro e responsabile da medici, studenti di medici, cittadini/pazienti in contesti clinici, formativi e informativi.

endorsements.title: Designing and evaluating large language model-enabled clinical decision support for heart failure: a modular and risk-tiered framework
endorsements.quote: Diagnostic outputs should be compared with HF specialist adjudication supported by final clinical diagnosis, echocardiography, natriuretic peptides, and follow-up data.

evidence.title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Capture of physician-consensus must-not-miss diagnoses in top three differential
evidence.effect: AegisDx captured at least one must-not-miss condition in top three in 78.0% of cases versus 52.0% for standalone LLM.
evidence.quote: against physician-consensus must-not-miss diagnosis sets, AegisDx captured at least one such condition among its top three diagnoses in 78.0% of cases versus 52.0%.
evidence.sample_unit: real-world emergency department notes (blinded physician evaluation)

evidence.title: Potential Use of ChatGPT for the Treatment of Infectious Diseases in Vulnerable Populations
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM antibiotic choice, dose and duration answers in special populations
evidence.effect: Comprehensive and correct: 38.1% pregnancy, 36.1% allergy, 27.5% older adults; error rates 11.9% pregnancy, 18.1% allergy, 25% older adults, 79.2% kidney disease, 43.8% children.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT produced high rates of inaccurate information for treating infectious diseases in special population.

evidence.title: Baseline Evaluation of Claude Opus 4 for Diabetes Management: A Preliminary Assessment and Lessons for Implementation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of clinical knowledge against ADA guidelines graded by endocrinologists
evidence.effect: 80% accuracy in general diabetes knowledge; mean expert rating of 4.4/7 on clinical cases, described as moderate utility.
evidence.quote: Clinical case evaluations showed moderate utility (mean expert rating = 4.4/7), while emotional-support assessments yielded high scores for empathy (6.2/7) and appropriateness (6.0/7).

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT's Compliance with ESC-Acute Coronary Syndrome Management Guidelines at 30-Day Intervals
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT clinical knowledge accuracy against 2023 ESC ACS guidelines
evidence.effect: Binary accuracy 84% initially and 86% at 30 days; multiple-choice 80% initially and 84% at 30 days. Errors and hallucinations remain a concern.
evidence.quote: For binary questions, accuracy was 84% initially and 86% after 30 days, with no significant change (p = 0.564).

evidence.title: Dental Trauma Evo - Development of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Chatbot to Support Professional Management of Dental Trauma
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of chatbot dental trauma management recommendations against IADT guidelines
evidence.effect: 100% accuracy in recommending appropriate management; initial completeness as low as 53% for primary tooth fractures, improved to 100% in most cases after code adjustments; avulsed open-apex reimplantation reached 93%.
evidence.quote: The chatbot achieved 100% accuracy in recommending appropriate clinical management.

evidence.title: Comparing Chinese-language large language models for caregiver questions about developmental dysplasia of the hip
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated clinical accuracy and concordance with Chinese DDH guidelines of LLM responses
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 higher accuracy than ChatGPT-4o (4.70 vs 3.69, P<0.001) and higher guideline concordance (4.44 vs 3.82, P<0.001); ChatGPT-4o lower on both.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-R1 had higher clinical accuracy than ChatGPT-4o across 31 caregiver-oriented questions (mean question-level score 4.70 [SD 0.15] vs. 3.69 [0.28]; P < 0.001) and higher guideline concordance across 22 items (4.44 [0.22] vs. 3.82 [0.33]; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: A ‘Silent Trial’ Assessing the Accuracy of Large Language Models for Assisting Community Health Workers in Low-Resource Settings
evidence.outcome: Completeness of LLM-generated differential diagnoses and management plans
evidence.effect: o3 outperformed Gemini on differential diagnosis and management plan quality, though both models missed important conditions.
evidence.quote: Assessment of LLM-generated differential diagnoses and management plan quality showed superior performance from o3 compared with Gemini, though both models missed important conditions.

evidence.title: Appropriateness and utility of a clinical decision support system at the digital front door
evidence.outcome: Inclusion of the treating physician’s most probable diagnosis among suggested conditions
evidence.effect: The physician’s most probable diagnosis was included in 80.4% (131/163; 95% CI 73.5–86.0) and omitted in 19.6% (32/163; 95% CI 14.0–26.5).
evidence.quote: The physician’s most probable diagnosis was included among the suggested conditions in 80.4% (131/163; 95% CI 73.5–86.0), with significant differences by specialty ( p = 0.035), but no significant variation by sex ( p = 1.000) or age group ( p = 0.191) (Supplementary Table 5 ).

evidence.title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: Screening recommendation concordance with current guidelines
evidence.effect: Guideline-concordant screening recommendations: 50 (100); unsafe or inappropriate outputs: 0 (0). Safety was assessed through expert review rather than downstream patient outcomes.
evidence.quote: Expert review confirmed that all chatbot-generated screening recommendations were consistent with current screening guidelines, and no inappropriate or unsafe outputs were identified during the study period.

evidence.title: Cognitive bias in LLM reasoning compromises interpretation of clinical oncology notes
evidence.outcome: Guideline-discordant and potentially harmful recommendations associated with reasoning errors in oncology
evidence.effect: Reasoning errors occurred in 23 percent of interpretations; reasoning failures were associated with guideline-discordant and potentially harmful recommendations, particularly in advanced disease management.
evidence.quote: Reasoning failures were associated with guideline-discordant and potentially harmful recommendations, particularly in advanced disease management.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses to prostate cancer consult notes

evidence.title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
evidence.outcome: Frequency and severity of harmful errors, especially omissions, in LLM consultation recommendations
evidence.effect: Direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.
evidence.quote: Across 20 notable LLMs and 4 widely used retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) clinical AI tools, direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.

evidence.title: Clinical Validation of Medical-based Large Language Model Chatbots on Ophthalmic Patient Queries with LLM-based Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Rate of hallucinations or clinically misleading content in medical LLM ophthalmic answers
evidence.effect: MedLLaMA3-v20 had 25.5 percent of responses containing hallucinations or clinically misleading content, including fabricated terminology; gaps remained in clinical depth and consensus.
evidence.quote: MedLLaMA3-v20 performed poorest, with 25.5 percent of responses containing hallucinations or clinically misleading content, including fabricated terminology.
evidence.sample_unit: model responses to ophthalmology patient queries

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Neuro-Oncology: Assessing ChatGPT’s Accuracy in MRI Interpretation and Treatment Advice
evidence.outcome: Differential diagnosis inclusion of correct tumor type on MRI interpretation by ChatGPT-4o
evidence.effect: Meningioma in differential for 73.3% of meningioma cases; glioma in 83.3% of glioblastoma cases; tumor localized correctly in 66.7% of cases.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT included meningioma in the differential diagnosis for 73.3% of meningioma cases and glioma in 83.3% of glioblastoma cases.
evidence.sample_unit: cases (90 MRI images, three planes per case)

evidence.title: Close, But no Cigar: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o and OpenAI o1-preview in Answering Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma-Related Questions
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy, comprehensiveness and safety on NCCN-guideline PDAC clinical questions, including critical errors
evidence.effect: o1-preview accuracy 75% vs 60% for ChatGPT-4o; both made critical errors in complex scenarios and caused some potential harm to patients.
evidence.quote: However, both models made critical errors in some complex clinical scenarios.

evidence.title: Feeding Intelligence: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT and Clinical Guidelines for Nutritional Management in Head and Neck Cancer
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT nutrition recommendations with CSCO, CNS and ESPEN guidelines
evidence.effect: ChatGPT aligned with at least one guideline in 50.0–64.3% of cases (highest for dysphagia, 64.3%). Guidelines scored higher for evidence-based support (4.9/5) and clinical feasibility (4.7/5).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT recommendations aligned with at least one guideline in 50.0–64.3% of cases, highest for dysphagia (64.3%), and included general strategies such as small frequent meals, texture modification, hydration, and high-protein/high-calorie intake.
evidence.sample_unit: nutrition-related clinical issues (ChatGPT responses compared with guidelines; 5 expert raters)

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-5 Responses in Obstetric and Gynecological Emergencies: Concordance, Readability, and Clinical Reliability
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-5 emergency management responses with guidelines and specialist gold standard
evidence.effect: High agreement (5/5) in 5 scenarios (33.3%), moderate (4/5) in 7 (46.7%), low (≤3/5) in 3 (20.0%); omissions of scoring systems and mortality risk emphasis.
evidence.quote: High agreement (5/5) was observed in 5 scenarios (33.3%), moderate agreement (4/5) in 7 scenarios (46.7%), and low agreement (≤ 3/5) in 3 scenarios (20.0%).

evidence.title: The Promise and Peril of Large Language Models in Digital Health: GPT-4 Personalizes Cardiovascular Patient Education but Amplifies Gender Biases
evidence.outcome: Completeness of clinical content in GPT-4 sex-specific CVD education revisions
evidence.effect: Male-tailored versions often missed key clinical factors; 4 of 7 revisions failed to mention erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker, while female-tailored versions incorporated biological facts such as menopause.
evidence.quote: For instance, 4 of 7 revisions failed to mention erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker.

evidence.title: Accuracy Assessment of Chinese Large Language Models in Psoriasis Management: A Multicenter Expert Consensus Study
evidence.outcome: Deviation of LLM responses from evidence-based guidelines on psoriasis questions
evidence.effect: 12.5% of responses deviated from evidence-based guidelines, particularly on complex topics like biologics and management; mean scores ranged from 5.95 to 9.88.
evidence.quote: However, 12.5% of responses deviated from evidence-based guidelines, particularly on complex topics like biologics and management.

evidence.title: Assessment of Professional Medical Capabilities in Mainstream Chinese Large Language Models for Tremor-Related Diseases: A Comparative Study Based on Expert Scoring
evidence.outcome: Expert-scored clinical knowledge accuracy of LLM answers on tremor-related diseases
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1-671B scored 9.1 ± 0.33, Doubao-1.5-pro-256k 6.8 ± 1.65, Moonshot-v1-128k-vision-preview 4.9 ± 1.02 (P < 0.05); one potentially harmful treatment response from Moonshot.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-R1-671B demonstrated the best performance (mean score 9.1 ± 0.33), significantly outperforming Doubao-1.5-pro-256k (6.8 ± 1.65) and Moonshot-v1-128k-vision-preview (4.9 ± 1.02) (P < 0.05).

evidence.title: Persona routing reduces safety and monotonicity violations in simulated emergency clinical reasoning with large language models
evidence.outcome: Contraindication/sequence safety violations in LLM emergency clinical reasoning by persona
evidence.effect: Lean baseline BASE_HL had safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; mean severity 0.39); SAFE baselines and routers had zero violations.
evidence.quote: The lean baseline (BASE_HL) suggested the fewest tests (mean 1.95) but had safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; mean severity 0.39).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated emergency vignette scenarios (28 vignettes x 2 replicates)

evidence.title: Prompting is All You Need: How to Make LLMs More Helpful for Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: LLM guideline adherence and unsafe thrombolysis recommendations by model
evidence.effect: Under simple prompts, some models made unsafe recommendations (16.7%). Llama-4-Scout and Llama-3.3-70B still had guideline adherence of 66.7% and unsafe recommendations of 33.3% with structured prompts.
evidence.quote: In contrast, other open-source models (Llama-4-Scout, Llama-3.3-70B) showed more modest gains: risk recognition improved (83.3% to 100%) and guideline grading accuracy increased (0% to 66.7%), while guideline adherence (66.7%) and unsafe recommendations (33.3%) persisted.

evidence.title: Boundary-Specific Failure Modes and Safety Trade-offs of Large Language Models in Chronic Kidney Disease Renoprotective Therapy Review: A Stratified Synthetic Benchmark
evidence.outcome: Clinically incorrect reasoning and pharmacology errors in LLM outputs
evidence.effect: Clinically incorrect reasoning ranged from 0% (GPT-5.4) to 27% (DeepSeek R1); of 52 instances, 31 were factual pharmacology errors and 21 conservative boundary-discordant reasoning.
evidence.quote: Clinically incorrect reasoning rates ranged from 0% (GPT-5.4) to 27% (DeepSeek R1); of 52 instances, 31 were factual pharmacology errors and 21 reflected conservative boundary-discordant reasoning.

evidence.title: Evaluating the AI Potential as a Safety Net for Diagnosis: A Novel Benchmark of Large Language Models in Correcting Diagnostic Errors
evidence.outcome: LLM ability to correct erroneous physician diagnosis across high-stakes conditions
evidence.effect: Correction rates ranged from 20.0% (DeepSeek V3) to 55.0% (Gemini 2.5 Pro); most models failed to correct errors in syphilis, spinal epidural abscess, and myocardial infarction.
evidence.quote: Performance was strikingly consistent at the disease level; most models failed to correct errors in syphilis, spinal epidural abscess, and myocardial infarction.

evidence.title: Dissecting clinical reasoning failures in frontier artificial intelligence using 10,000 synthetic cases
evidence.outcome: Clinically appropriate steroid and thrombolysis recommendations by LLMs for MS cases
evidence.effect: Appropriate steroid recommendations: Gemini Flash 7.2%, Pro 15.8%, GPT-5-mini 23.5%. Inappropriate thrombolysis: GPT-5.2 9.6%, GPT-5-mini 6.4%, Gemini models <1%.
evidence.quote: Gemini 3 models had low rates of clinically appropriate steroid recommendations (Flash: 7.2% [95% CI 5.6–8.8]; Pro: 15.8% [13.6–18.1]) compared to GPT-5-mini (23.5% [20.8–26.1]), frequently overlooking contraindications like active infection.

evidence.title: A Systematic Performance Evaluation of Three Large Language Models in Answering Questions on moderate Hyperthermia
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated quality and potential harmfulness of LLM answers to hyperthermia clinical and physics questions
evidence.effect: Mean quality 3.26 (DeepSeek), 3.18 (Llama), 3.07 (GPT-4o); potentially harmful in 17.8%, 19.3%, 15.3% of cases; ~25% rated bad to very bad.
evidence.quote: Notably, despite “acceptable” mean scores, approximately 25% of responses were rated “bad” to “very bad,” and potentially harmful answers occurred in ∼15–19% of evaluations, indicating a non-trivial risk if used without domain expertise.
evidence.sample_unit: expert quality evaluations of LLM responses

evidence.title: A Chatbot for the Management of Bipolar Disorder: Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation with an Open-Weight Large Language Model to Answer Clinical Questions Based on the CANMAT and ISBD 2018 Guidelines for Bipolar Disorder
evidence.outcome: guideline deviations in clinical answers
evidence.effect: Major deviations occurred in 10 RAG answers (7.9%) and 48 baseline answers (38.1%).
evidence.quote: The RAG system produced 80 answers (63.5%) rated fully consistent with the guidelines versus 24 (19.0%) for baseline, and only 10 answers with major deviation (7.9%) versus 48 (38.1%) for baseline.

evidence.title: Comparative Benchmarking of Five Contemporary Language Models on Clinical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and contraindication handling in clinical vignettes
evidence.effect: Kimi K2 Thinking and ChatGPT-5.2 showed 100% diagnostic accuracy and perfect safety adherence; Gemini 3 Pro and Claude 4.5 Opus recommended carbapenems in severe penicillin anaphylaxis, missing the contraindication.
evidence.quote: Kimi K2 Thinking and ChatGPT-5.2 achieved the highest aggregate scores (3.50/3.50), demonstrating 100% diagnostic accuracy and perfect safety adherence.

evidence.title: Blinded Expert Evaluation of Large Language Models for Osteoporosis Case Management in Older Adults: Impact of Direct Guideline Integration
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated guideline adherence and contraindication awareness of LLM osteoporosis recommendations
evidence.effect: Panels differed in scientific accuracy (p=0.0006) and guideline compliance (p<0.0001); safety/contraindications awareness was the lowest-rated criterion in base models.
evidence.quote: Safety/contraindications awareness was lowest-rated criterion in base models.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (25 hypothetical cases x 4 panels)

evidence.title: Can Large Language Models Assist Surgeons in Managing Implant-Related Complications? A Guideline-Informed Comparative Evaluation
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and management completeness against guideline-informed scenarios
evidence.effect: Models differed significantly (completeness/actionability p = 0.001; diagnostic accuracy p = 0.023). Gemini 3.1 scored 4.30 vs DeepSeek V3.2 3.58 overall (adjusted p = 0.003). Differences appeared only in difficult scenarios.
evidence.quote: After Holm correction, Gemini 3.1 scored significantly higher than DeepSeek V3.2 in all domains and overall (4.30 vs 3.58; adjusted p = 0.003); no other comparisons were significant.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Masks Outdated Reasoning: Evaluating LLMs on Evolving Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated validity of stated clinical rationale despite correct conclusions
evidence.effect: Stated clinical rationale valid in only 53.7% of responses despite near-ceiling conclusion accuracy; qSOFA-as-diagnostic and lactate-as-organ-dysfunction conflations.
evidence.quote: a blinded physician review, corroborated by a second independent reviewer, found the stated clinical rationale valid in only 53.7% of responses despite near-ceiling conclusion accuracy

evidence.title: Research Letter: Application of GPT-4 to select next-step antidepressant treatment in major depression
evidence.outcome: Inclusion of poor or contraindicated antidepressants among choices GPT-4 considered optimal or good
evidence.effect: Poor or contraindicated medications were included among optimal/good choices in 24/50 (48%) of vignettes; at least one optimal choice was included in 38/50 (76%), with 0/5 for 2 vignettes.
evidence.quote: At least one of the poor choice or contraindicated medications was included among the choices considered optimal or good in 24/50 (48%) of vignettes.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT as an Adjunct for the Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making in Primary Breast Cancer Cases
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT therapy recommendations versus tumor board decisions for early breast cancer
evidence.effect: ChatGPT gave mostly general answers, wrongly recommended trastuzumab for Her2 1+ and 2+ (FISH negative) patient; current version unable to provide specific therapy recommendations.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT wrongly identified the patient with Her2 1+ and 2+ (FISH negative) as in need of therapy with trastuzumab and called endocrine therapy “hormonal treatment”.
evidence.sample_unit: patient cases (consecutive early breast cancer cases discussed at tumor board)

evidence.title: “Assessing ChatGPT's Performance in Answering Cervical Cancer Screening Questions to ChatGPT-generated Clinical Vignettes: A Pilot Study”
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of cervical cancer screening answers compared with current standard of care
evidence.effect: Of 5 vignettes, 1 answer was unsatisfactory, 2 were acceptable and 2 were satisfactory against the current standard of care.
evidence.quote: The answer was found to be unsatisfactory for one vignette, acceptable for two, and satisfactory for two when compared with the current standard of care.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated clinical vignettes with queries and answers

evidence.title: Accuracy and Consistency of Online Chat-based Artificial Intelligence Platforms in Answering Patients’ Questions About Heart Failure
evidence.outcome: Expert-graded adequacy of chatbot answers to heart failure questions, including contemporary recommendations
evidence.effect: ChatGPT appropriate in 27/30 (90%); Bard 23/30 (77%). Both had hallucinated facts and/or difficulty with more contemporary recommendations.
evidence.quote: Both platforms suffered from issues related to “hallucination” of facts and/or difficulty with more contemporary recommendations.

evidence.title: Advancing Rheumatology Practice with AI Assistance: Evaluating ChatGPT's Performance in Real-world Cases
evidence.outcome: Correctness and completeness of ChatGPT differential diagnosis lists in rheumatology cases
evidence.effect: Correct diagnosis listed first in 65.6% of cases; differential diagnosis totally correct in 53.13% and totally complete in 62.50% of instances; no harmful or costly suggestions.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT was successful in 65.6% of the cases to suggest the correct diagnosis first in the list of differential diagnoses.

evidence.title: Examining the Accuracy and Reproducibility of Responses to Nutrition Questions Related to Inflammatory Bowel Disease by Generative Pre-trained Transformer-4 (GPT-4)
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of GPT-4 nutrition answers graded by dietitians against current knowledge
evidence.effect: 73/88 (83.0%) correct, 61 (69.0%) comprehensive; 15/88 (17%) mixed with correct and incorrect/outdated data.
evidence.quote: 15/88 (17%) responses were graded as mixed with correct and incorrect/outdated data.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT as an Agent for Providing Genetic Education
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT answers to genetic disorder questions, as rated by genetic experts
evidence.effect: ChatGPT answered 64.7% of the 68 genetic questions; limitations and inaccuracies noted, particularly in understanding human inheritance patterns.
evidence.quote: Here we show that ChatGPT answered 64.7% of the 68 genetic questions asked and was able to respond coherently to complex questions related to the three genes/conditions.

evidence.title: ChatGPT Exhibits Gender and Racial Biases in Acute Coronary Syndrome Management
evidence.outcome: guideline-recommended ACS care
evidence.effect: Female, African American, or Hispanic patient specification decreased guideline-recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.
evidence.quote: We find that specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic resulted in a decrease in guideline recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.

evidence.title: Evaluating and Mitigating Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Making
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and adherence to diagnostic and treatment guidelines on real abdominal cases
evidence.effect: LLMs did not diagnose accurately across all pathologies, performed significantly worse than physicians on average, followed neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and could not interpret laboratory results.
evidence.quote: We show that current state-of-the-art LLMs do not accurately diagnose patients across all pathologies (performing significantly worse than physicians on average), follow neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and cannot interpret laboratory results, thus posing a serious risk to the health of patients.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT’s Accuracy in Providing Screening Mammography Recommendations among Older Women: Artificial Intelligence and Cancer Communication
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT breast cancer screening answers for women 75+, graded by expert panel
evidence.effect: Appropriate for 11/17 questions (64%); 3 inappropriate (18%), 2 unreliable (12%), 1 no consensus (6%).
evidence.quote: The responses generated by ChatGPT were appropriate for 11/17 questions (64%).
evidence.sample_unit: questions (12 questions and 4 vignettes as reported; 17 graded)

evidence.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness and Safety of Large Language Model in Generating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Plans: A Comparative Study with Medical Experts Based on Real Patient Records
evidence.outcome: Completeness of GPT-4 management plans versus ADA guideline reference plan (missing medications)
evidence.effect: Medical experts' plans had fewer missing medications than GPT-4's (p=0.008). Safety issues appeared in 16% of GPT-4 plans.
evidence.quote: Safety issues were noted in 16% of the plans generated by GPT-4, highlighting potential risks associated with AI-generated management plans.

evidence.title: Assessing the potential of ChatGPT-4 to accurately identify drug-drug interactions and provide clinical pharmacotherapy recommendations
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of GPT-4 clinical recommendations for drug-drug interaction regimens
evidence.effect: Inappropriate recommendations potentially causing harm in 14% of responses (2/14); 63% (19/30) accurate but incomplete; intended DDI identified in 90% (27/30).
evidence.quote: Inappropriate clinical recommendations potentially causing patient harm were provided in 14% of responses provided by GPT-4 (2/14), and 63% of responses contained accurate information but incomplete recommendations (19/30).
evidence.sample_unit: GPT-4 responses (15 medication regimens x 2 prompts)

evidence.title: Potentials and pitfalls of ChatGPT and natural-language artificial intelligence models for the understanding of laboratory medicine test results. An assessment by the European Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (EFLM) Working Group on Artificial Intelligence (WG-AI)
evidence.outcome: Correctness and completeness of ChatGPT interpretation of simulated lab reports, including follow-up suggestions
evidence.effect: Interpretations were superficial, not always correct, only sometimes coherent; magnitude of deviation from reference interval seldom mattered; no meaningful follow-up diagnostics suggested.
evidence.quote: The interpretations were rather superficial, not always correct, and, only in some cases, judged coherently.

evidence.title: Appropriateness and Readability of ChatGPT-4-Generated Responses for Surgical Treatment of Retinal Diseases
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT-4 clinical answers on retinal surgery graded by retina specialists
evidence.effect: Consistently appropriate in 84.6% (33/39) RD, 92% (23/25) MH, 91.7% (22/24) ERM; inappropriate at least once in 5.1%, 8%, 8.3%.
evidence.quote: Responses were consistently appropriate in 84.6% (33/39), 92% (23/25), and 91.7% (22/24) of the questions related to RD, MH, and ERM, respectively.

evidence.title: Exploring ChatGPT's Potential in Facilitating Adaptation of Clinical Guidelines: A Case Study of Diabetic Ketoacidosis Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Misreporting and non-reporting errors in ChatGPT-synthesized DKA guideline comparison
evidence.effect: Multiple recurrent misreporting and non-reporting errors were identified, rendering the results unreliable; no numeric error rates reported.
evidence.quote: However, multiple recurrent errors, including misreporting and non-reporting errors, were identified, rendering the results unreliable.

evidence.title: Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Chatbot for Delivery of IR Patient Education Material: A Comparison with Societal Website Content
evidence.venue: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
evidence.outcome: Factual correctness of ChatGPT answers to interventional radiology patient questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT output was incorrect for 12 (11.5%) of 104 questions; PEMAT-P scores lower than website.
evidence.quote: The ChatGPT output was incorrect for 12 (11.5%) of 104 questions.

evidence.title: ChatGPT in glioma adjuvant therapy decision making: ready to assume the role of a doctor in the tumour board?
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated quality of ChatGPT glioma diagnosis and adjuvant treatment recommendations
evidence.effect: Diagnosis rated poor (median 3, IQR 1-7.8); treatment recommendation good (7, IQR 6-8); therapy regimen good (7, IQR 4-8); overall agreement moderate (5, IQR 3-7).
evidence.quote: The experts rated the quality of ChatGPT recommendations as poor for diagnosis (median 3, IQR 1-7.8, ICC 0.9, 95% CI 0.7 to 1.0), good for treatment recommendation (7, IQR 6-8, ICC 0.8, 95% CI 0.4 to 0.9), good for therapy regimen (7, IQR 4-8, ICC 0.8, 95% CI 0.5 to 0.9), moderate for functional status consideration (6, IQR 1-7, ICC 0.7, 95% CI 0.3 to 0.9) and moderate for overall agreement with the recommendations (5, IQR 3-7, ICC 0.7, 95% CI 0.3 to 0.9).

evidence.title: Examining Real-World Medication Consultations and Drug-Herb Interactions: ChatGPT Performance Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT medication consultation responses rated by pharmacists
evidence.effect: Appropriateness was higher for public questions than for health care provider questions (31/51, 61% vs 20/51, 39%; P=.01), showing many inappropriate responses. Erroneous information was linked to potential medical risks.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT exhibited a higher appropriateness rate in responding to public medication consultation questions compared to those asked by health care providers in a hospital setting (31/51, 61% vs 20/51, 39%; P=.01).

evidence.title: Can artificial intelligence replace biochemists? A study comparing interpretation of thyroid function test results by ChatGPT and Google Bard to practising biochemists
evidence.outcome: Correct interpretation of thyroid function test cases versus clinician consensus
evidence.effect: ChatGPT and Google Bard correctly interpreted only 33.3% and 20.0% of 15 cases; both failed to identify subclinical presentations, non-thyroidal illness or secondary hypothyroidism.
evidence.quote: Of the 15 cases presented, ChatGPT and Google Bard correctly interpreted only 33.3% and 20.0% of cases, respectively.

evidence.title: The potential of chatbots in chronic venous disease patient management
evidence.outcome: Grading of chatbot answers to complex chronic venous disease questions by two specialists
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 4.0 grade 1 on 15/20 (75%), grade 4 on 1/20 (5%); ChatGPT 3.5 grade 1 on 9/20 (45%), grade 4 on 3/20 (15%); Clinical Camel grade 1 on 0/20, grade 4 on 10/20 (50%).
evidence.quote: Clinical Camel received a grade of 1 on 0 of 20 questions (0%), grade 2 on 5 of 20 questions (25%), grade 3 on 5 of 20 questions (25%), and grade 4 on 10 of 20 questions (50%).

evidence.title: Preliminary assessment of automated radiology report generation with generative pre-trained transformers: comparing results to radiologist-generated reports
evidence.outcome: Differential diagnosis accuracy (top-1, top-5) of GPT models versus radiologists
evidence.effect: Top-1: radiologists 1.00, GPT-4 0.54, GPT-3.5 0.54, GPT-2 0.21; Top-5: 1.00, 0.96, 0.89, 0.54. GPT impression and differential diagnosis scores significantly lower than radiologists (p<0.05).
evidence.quote: However, qualitative scores of the GPT series in impression and differential diagnosis scores were significantly lower than those of radiologists (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: The Potential of ChatGPT as a Self-Diagnostic Tool in Common Orthopedic Diseases: Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT for common orthopedic conditions
evidence.effect: Correct answers 25/25 CTS, 1/25 CM, 24/25 LSS, 16/25 KOA, 17/25 HOA; 23/25 incorrect for CM.
evidence.quote: The ratios of correct answers were 25/25, 1/25, 24/25, 16/25, and 17/25 for CTS, CM, LSS, KOA, and HOA, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT answers (5 conditions x 5 raters x 5 days)

evidence.title: Can Chatbot Artificial Intelligence Replace Infectious Diseases Physicians in the Management of Bloodstream Infections? A Prospective Cohort Study
evidence.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
evidence.outcome: Adequacy of ChatGPT-4 diagnosis, workup, and antibiotic plans versus ID consultants
evidence.effect: Diagnoses identical in 26 (59%); empirical therapy adequate in 28 (64%), harmful in 1 (2%); definitive therapy optimal in 16 (36%), harmful in 2 (5%); overall plans harmful in 7 (16%).
evidence.quote: Overall, management plans were considered optimal in only 1 patient, as satisfactory in 17 (39%), and as harmful in 7 (16%).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (consecutive ID consultations for first positive blood culture)

evidence.title: ChatGPT performance in laryngology and head and neck surgery: a clinical case-series
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT differential diagnosis completeness and omission of important additional examinations in LHN cases
evidence.effect: Highest performance for primary (90%) and most plausible differential diagnoses (65%); additional examinations lowest; ChatGPT never indicated PET-CT, voice quality assessment, or impedance-pH monitoring.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT never indicated some important additional examinations (PET-CT, voice quality assessment, or impedance-pH monitoring).

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Therapy Recommendations Across 3 Clinical Specialties: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Correctness, omissions and harmfulness of LLM therapy recommendations rated by physicians
evidence.effect: Significant differences in falseness across models and specialties (P<.001); errors included confusing diagnoses, vague advice, omitting critical treatments such as antibiotics for infectious diseases.
evidence.quote: Distinct error patterns emerged, such as confusing diagnoses; providing vague, ambiguous advice; or omitting critical treatments, such as antibiotics for infectious diseases.

evidence.title: Quality and Agreement With Scientific Consensus of ChatGPT Information Regarding Corneal Transplantation and Fuchs Dystrophy
evidence.outcome: Responses judged against scientific consensus by corneal specialists
evidence.effect: 35% of ChatGPT-3.5 responses were against scientific consensus, decreasing to 5% for GPT-4 (P<0.00001); average grade 2.5 vs 1.4.
evidence.quote: Approximately a third (35%) of responses from ChatGPT-3.5 were considered against the scientific consensus, a notable rate of error that decreased to only 5% of answers from GPT-4 ( P < 0.00001).
evidence.sample_unit: valid responses rated by corneal specialists

evidence.title: Accuracy and comprehensibility of chat-based artificial intelligence for patient information on atrial fibrillation and cardiac implantable electronic devices
evidence.venue: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness and completeness of chatbot answers on AF and CIED questions
evidence.effect: Fully appropriate responses: AF 52% (Bard), 60% (Bing), 84% (ChatGPT Plus); CIEDs 16%, 72%, 88%. Relevant aspects missing: AF 52%, 60%, 24%; CIEDs 92%, 88%, 52%.
evidence.quote: Relevant aspects were missing in 52% (GB), 60% (BC), and 24% (CGP) for AF, and in 92% (GB), 88% (BC), and 52% (CGP) for CIEDs.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (25 AF and 25 CIED questions entered into each of three chatbots)

evidence.title: Comprehensiveness, Accuracy, and Readability of Exercise Recommendations Provided by an AI-Based Chatbot: Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Comprehensiveness and factual accuracy of AI exercise recommendations versus gold-standard guidelines
evidence.effect: Recommendations were 41.2% (107/260) comprehensive and 90.7% (146/161) accurate; most inaccuracy (8/15, 53%) related to preparticipation medical clearance.
evidence.quote: AI-generated exercise recommendations were 41.2% (107/260) comprehensive and 90.7% (146/161) accurate, with the majority (8/15, 53%) of inaccuracy related to the need for exercise preparticipation medical clearance.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence and ChatGPT: An otolaryngology patient's ally or foe?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT clinical content on ENT procedures (risks, steps, recovery)
evidence.effect: Appropriate treatment alternatives in all procedures; lacked precision in procedural steps, missed key surgical details, did not provide all major risks; total laryngectomy recovery wrongly said patient could speak immediately.
evidence.quote: When queried for methodology, risks, and procedural steps, ChatGPT lacked precision in the description of procedural steps, missed key surgical details, and did not accurately provide all major risks of each procedure.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (5 questions x 5 otolaryngologic procedures)

evidence.title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Rate of hallucinations and misinformation in ChatGPT reasoning on FFA reports
evidence.effect: Step-Chinese: hallucinations 5.88%, misinformation 7.84%; Step-English: 0.59% and 1.96%; 0.4 reasoning errors per report.
evidence.quote: Notably, although ChatGPT can derive a reasoning process to improve clinical interpretability, ophthalmologists identified some harmful mistakes, such as generating medical findings not mentioned in the original reports and quoting incorrect prior knowledge.

evidence.title: PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT OF AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CHATBOT IN CLINICAL VITREORETINAL SCENARIOS
evidence.outcome: Correctness and comprehensiveness of ChatGPT answers to vitreoretinal clinical scenarios
evidence.effect: Answered 83% (33/40) correctly but comprehensive in only 52.5% (21/40); six incorrect responses, three with possible harm and two with definitive harm.
evidence.quote: In June 2023, ChatGPT answered 83% of clinical scenarios (33/40) correctly but provided a comprehensive answer in only 52.5% of cases (21/40).

evidence.title: ChatGPT fails challenging the recent ESCMID brain abscess guideline
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT recommendations with ESCMID brain abscess guideline and patient hazard
evidence.effect: Without data prompting 70% of answers very similar to guideline, no patient hazard in differing answers; with data input, fewer correct answers including two recommendations directly contradicting guideline with possible patient hazard.
evidence.quote: Data input slightly improved the clarity of ChatGPT's recommendations, but, however, led to less correct answers including two recommendations that directly contradicted the guideline, being associated with the possibility of a hazard to the patient.
evidence.sample_unit: guideline PECO questions (20 challenges: with and without data prompting)

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT Compared to Clinical Practice Guidelines in Making Informed Decisions for Lumbosacral Radicular Pain: A Cross-sectional Study
evidence.venue: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT answers with clinical practice guideline recommendations for lumbosacral radicular pain
evidence.effect: Accuracy versus CPG recommendations was slight, with agreement in 33% of recommendations.
evidence.quote: Accuracy between ChatGPT answers and CPGs recommendations was slight, demonstrating agreement in 33% of recommendations.

evidence.title: Comparison of Large Language Models in Answering Immuno-Oncology Questions: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM answers to immuno-oncology questions
evidence.effect: Fully correct answers: 75.4% ChatGPT-4, 58.5% ChatGPT-3.5, 43.8% Google Bard (P = .03); risk of inaccuracy or incompleteness evident in all three LLMs.
evidence.quote: In terms of accuracy, the number of answers deemed fully correct were 75.4%, 58.5%, and 43.8% for ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5, and Google Bard, respectively (P = .03).

evidence.title: ChatGPT Provides Unsatisfactory Responses to Frequently Asked Questions Regarding Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
evidence.venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and currency of ChatGPT answers to ACL reconstruction FAQs
evidence.effect: 6 of 10 responses unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification; 1 adequate moderate clarification; 1 adequate minor; 2 satisfactory. Mean DISCERN score 41. Most responses were outdated.
evidence.quote: Of the 10 frequently asked questions entered into ChatGPT, 6 were deemed as unsatisfactory and requiring substantial clarification; 1, as adequate and requiring moderate clarification; 1, as adequate and requiring minor clarification; and 2, as satisfactory and requiring minimal clarification.

evidence.title: Large-Scale assessment of ChatGPT's performance in benign and malignant bone tumors imaging report diagnosis and its potential for clinical applications
evidence.outcome: Errors in differential diagnosis, missed serious conditions like malignancies
evidence.effect: ChatGPT misdiagnosed malignant tumors as benign or infection, e.g., 23 osteosarcoma as osteomyelitis, 8 chondrosarcoma as fibrous dysplasia or aneurysmal bone cyst; 56 benign cases labelled malignant.
evidence.quote: Chondrosarcoma was misdiagnosed as fibrous dysplasia or aneurysmal bone cyst in 8 cases.

evidence.title: Assessing the Accuracy of Information on Medication Abortion: A Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Bard AI
evidence.outcome: Accuracy (6-point) and completeness (3-point) of chatbot medication abortion answers versus NAF/RHAP/ACOG guidance
evidence.effect: ChatGPT median accuracy 5 (mean 5.26), completeness mean 2.57; Bard median accuracy 5 (mean 4.5), completeness mean 2.14; Bard gave no answer to 5 questions initially; no significant difference between chatbots.
evidence.quote: While both chatbots showed similar levels of accuracy, minor errors were noted, pertaining to finer aspects that demand specialized knowledge of abortion care.

evidence.title: Classification of posttransfusion adverse events using a publicly available artificial intelligence system
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI diagnosis of transfusion reaction categories versus expert panel and TM specialists
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 48.7% for AI versus 72.1% for prior TM specialist responses (p = 0.005); no correct identification in some NHSN categories such as DSTR.
evidence.quote: Overall accuracy among all diagnostic categories was 48.7% for AI responses versus 72.1% for prior TM specialist responses (p = 0.005).

evidence.title: The utility and accuracy of ChatGPT in providing post-operative instructions following tonsillectomy: A pilot study
evidence.outcome: Expert-panel accuracy of ChatGPT answers to post-tonsillectomy parent questions against clinical knowledge
evidence.effect: Pain management mean satisfaction 3.67 and follow-up 2.67 (of 5); recommended codeine for children despite black-box warning; suggested 1-week follow-up vs customary 2-4 weeks.
evidence.quote: Pain management and follow-up recommendations were inaccurate, including a recommendation to prescribe codeine to children despite a black-box warning, and a suggested post-operative follow-up at 1 week, rather than the customary 2-4 weeks for our panel.

evidence.title: Clinical decision support for bipolar depression using large language models
evidence.venue: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
evidence.outcome: Frequency of LLM selecting poor or contraindicated medications among top choices
evidence.effect: Augmented model selected at least one poor/contraindicated medication in 12.0% of vignettes; base model 10.8%; community clinicians 22-24%.
evidence.quote: Conversely, for 120 (12.0%) of vignettes, the model selected a medication considered by the experts to be a poor choice, or contraindicated.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical vignettes (each run 20 times, 1000 model outputs per condition)

evidence.title: Accuracy of Information given by ChatGPT for Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Relation to ECCO Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT answers versus ECCO guidelines rated by gastroenterologists
evidence.effect: 84.2% of replies had median accuracy ≥4; mean accuracy 3.87; mean completeness 2.24/3. Lowest ratings for malignancy screening and vaccination in immunosuppression and family planning.
evidence.quote: However, responses in specialist areas may deviate from evidence-based guidance and the replies need to give more firm advice.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the safety, accuracy, and helpfulness of the GPT-4.0 Large Language Model in neurosurgery
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
evidence.outcome: Consistency with current guidelines, incorporation of recent advances, and missed red-flag symptoms in neurosurgical answers
evidence.effect: Responses consistent with guidelines 92.8% and accounted for recent advances 78.6% of the time; red flag symptoms missed 7.1% of the time.
evidence.quote: GPT-4.0 responses were consistent with current medical guidelines and accounted for recent advances in the field 92.8 % and 78.6 % of the time respectively.

evidence.title: Can large language models provide secondary reliable opinion on treatment options for dermatological diseases?
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Dermatologist approval and database-associated accuracy of ChatGPT drug recommendations for common skin diseases
evidence.effect: 98.87% dermatologist approval; accuracy 95.14% at Q-value cutoff 3, 85.42% at 5, 72.92% at 10; occasional incorrect ATC codes.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT achieved a high 98.87% dermatologist approval rate for common dermatological medication recommendations.

evidence.title: Harnessing artificial intelligence in bariatric surgery: comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4, Bing, and Bard in generating clinician-level bariatric surgery recommendations
evidence.venue: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
evidence.outcome: Surgeon-rated appropriateness of LLM answers to guideline-based bariatric surgery questions
evidence.effect: Appropriate answers: ChatGPT-4 85.7%, Bard 74.3%, Bing 25.7% (P < .001); mean Likert 4.46, 3.89, 3.11.
evidence.quote: There was a significant difference between the 3 LLMs in the proportion of appropriate answers, with ChatGPT-4 at 85.7%, Bard at 74.3%, and Bing at 25.7% (P < .001).

evidence.title: ChatGPT's adherence to otolaryngology clinical practice guidelines
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT accuracy versus AAO-HNS clinical practice guidelines across otolaryngology subspecialties
evidence.effect: 59.7% (43/72) highly accurate; 2.8% (2/72) directly contradicted guidelines; accuracy 100% Head and Neck, 66% Rhinology and Otology, 50% Laryngology, 8% Pediatrics.
evidence.quote: The model showed 100% accuracy in Head and Neck, but lower accuracy in Rhinology and Otology/Neurotology (66%), Laryngology (50%), and Pediatrics (8%).

evidence.title: ChatGPT's Performance in Cardiac Arrest and Bradycardia Simulations Using the American Heart Association's Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support Guidelines: Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT adherence to 2020 AHA ACLS guidelines steps
evidence.effect: Median step accuracy 85% (IQR 40%-100%) cardiac arrest, 30% (IQR 13%-81%) bradycardia; per-attempt median 69% and 42%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's median accuracy over 20 simulation attempts for cardiac arrest was 69% (IQR 67%-74%) and for bradycardia was 42% (IQR 33%-50%).

evidence.title: A Comparative Study of Responses to Retina Questions from Either Experts, Expert-Edited Large Language Models, or Expert-Edited Large Language Models Alone
evidence.outcome: Clinical knowledge errors and missing content in LLM answers to retina questions
evidence.effect: LLMs produced incorrect or missing content, e.g. a generalized 3-month anti-VEGF interval and calling retinal vein occlusion an 'eye stroke'; Bard and Bing had the highest proportion of high-risk responses.
evidence.quote: An LLM suggested a generalized 3-month interval between anti-VEGF injections for most patients, disregarding individual patient needs.

evidence.title: Local large language models for privacy-preserving accelerated review of historic echocardiogram reports
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: LLM answer accuracy against cardiologist ground truth on echocardiogram report questions
evidence.effect: LLM correctly answered 90% of questions: 83% temporality, 93% severity assessment, 84% intervention identification, 100% diagnosis retrieval.
evidence.quote: The LLM correctly answered 90% questions, with accuracies of 83% for temporality, 93% for severity assessment, 84% for intervention identification, and 100% for diagnosis retrieval.

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT-4 to Analyze 24-Hour Urine Results and Generate Custom Dietary Recommendations for Nephrolithiasis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, completeness and appropriateness of LLM dietary advice for urine abnormalities, rated by experts
evidence.effect: Average scores 5.2/6 accuracy, 2.4/3 completeness, 2.6/3 appropriateness; poor on calcium and citrate abnormalities; failed to address 3/10 abnormalities entirely.
evidence.quote: The model performed particularly poorly in response to calcium and citrate abnormalities and failed to address 3/10 abnormalities entirely.

evidence.title: The Use of Chatbots in Head and Neck Mucosal Malignancy Treatment Recommendations
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT staging and treatment recommendations versus NCCN guidelines, including omitted neck dissection
evidence.effect: 95% accurate for first-line treatment; 55% inaccurate staging; neck dissection omitted in 50%; 40% of treatment recommendations deemed unnecessary.
evidence.quote: Whereas ChatGPT's responses were 95% accurate at recommending the correct first-line treatment based on the 2021 NCCN guidelines, 55% of the responses contained inaccurate staging.

evidence.title: Evaluation of GPT-4 ability to identify and generate patient instructions for actionable incidental radiology findings
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 hallucinations and inferred recommendations in generated text
evidence.effect: No findings hallucinated outright; 2.8% of cases included generated text about recommendations inferred without specific reference.
evidence.quote: No findings were "hallucinated" outright. However, 2.8% of cases included generated text about recommendations that were inferred without specific reference.

evidence.title: Use of artificial intelligence chatbots in clinical management of immune-related adverse events
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of chatbot answers to irAE guideline questions
evidence.effect: Accuracy 3.87 (ChatGPT) vs 3.5 (Bard), p<0.01; completeness 3.83 vs 3.46; scores of 1-2 rare for ChatGPT (6/800, 0.75%); patient scenarios accuracy 3.725, completeness 3.61.
evidence.quote: Overall, both engines scored highly for accuracy (mean scores for ChatGPT and Bard were 3.87 vs 3.5, p<0.01) and completeness (3.83 vs 3.46, p<0.01).
evidence.sample_unit: questions (plus 20 patient scenarios), rated by 8 physician experts

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-Generated Educational Patient Pamphlets for Common Interventional Radiology Procedures
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT-generated IR procedure pamphlets reviewed by two radiologists
evidence.effect: Shortcomings in 30% (30/100) of pamphlets, with 34 specific inaccuracies, including missing sedation information (10/34) and inaccurate procedural complication details (8/34).
evidence.quote: In a thorough analysis of the education pamphlets, we identified shortcomings in 30% (30/100) of pamphlets, with a total of 34 specific inaccuracies, including missing information about sedation for the procedure (10/34), inaccuracies related to specific procedural-related complications (8/34).

evidence.title: Assessing the role of advanced artificial intelligence as a tool in multidisciplinary tumor board decision-making for primary head and neck cancer cases
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM treatment recommendations with current guidelines and tumor board decisions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 suggested significantly more therapy options than the MDT; some recommended modalities, such as primary immunotherapy, are not part of current treatment guidelines.
evidence.quote: For clinical recommendation, explanation and summarization ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 scored well, but demonstrated to be mostly an assisting tool, suggesting significantly more therapy options than our MDT, while some of the recommended treatment modalities like primary immunotherapy are not part of the current treatment guidelines.
evidence.sample_unit: consecutive head and neck cancer patients discussed at tumor board

evidence.title: A comparative evaluation of ChatGPT 3.5 and ChatGPT 4 in responses to selected genetics questions
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of GPT-4 genetics answers, including outdated information
evidence.effect: GPT-4 was more accurate than GPT-3.5 (P < .0001), but notable accuracy errors remained and outdated information was a challenge.
evidence.quote: The study underscores GPT-4's potential role in genetic education, showing notable progress yet facing challenges like outdated information and the necessity of ongoing refinement.

evidence.title: Evaluation of a Large Language Model's Ability to Assist in an Orthopedic Hand Clinic
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and differential/workup/treatment quality of ChatGPT on hand pathology vignettes
evidence.effect: Diagnostic accuracy 7 of 9 (78%); less reliable with complex or uncommon pathologies. Workup rated 4.1 ± 1.0, treatment plan 4.3 ± 0.8.
evidence.quote: The diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT was 7 out of 9 cases, indicating an overall accuracy rate of 78%.

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-Generated Differential Diagnosis for Common Diseases With Atypical Presentation: Descriptive Research
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT top 1 and top 5 differential diagnoses with final diagnosis by atypicality category
evidence.effect: Category 1: top 1 17% (n=1), top 5 67% (n=4). Categories 3 and 4: 0% top 1 and markedly lower top 5. Top 5 accuracy differed significantly between less and more atypical cases (P=.048); top 1 did not (P=.13).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's diagnostic accuracy decreased with an increase in atypical presentation.

evidence.title: Assessing large language models' accuracy in providing patient support for choroidal melanoma
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of LLM answers to choroidal melanoma patient medical advice questions
evidence.effect: For medical advice questions, ChatGPT gave 92% accurate responses compared to 58% for Bing AI and DocsGPT; pre/post-op accuracy 86% (ChatGPT, Bing AI) and 73% (DocsGPT); no statistically significant differences between models.
evidence.quote: For medical advice questions, ChatGPT gave 92% accurate responses compared to 58% for Bing AI and DocsGPT.

evidence.title: TrachGPT: Appraisal of tracheostomy care recommendations from an artificial intelligent Chatbot
evidence.outcome: Clinical appropriateness and accuracy of ChatGPT tracheostomy care responses graded by otolaryngologists
evidence.effect: Appropriateness mean 4.10 (SD 0.90) of 5, accuracy 3.55 (SD 0.50) of 4, overall 4.02 (SD 0.86); suboptimal responses lacked nuance and contained incorrect information.
evidence.quote: Suboptimal responses lacked nuance and contained incorrect information and recommendations.

evidence.title: Evaluating Chatbot responses to patient questions in the field of glaucoma
evidence.outcome: Expert-graded accuracy and comprehensiveness of ChatGPT glaucoma answers (1-4 scale)
evidence.effect: Mean panel score 3.29 (SD 0.484); 7 of 24 (29.2%) question-response pairs had mean inter-grader score of 3 or less, so most were adequate but a substantial minority incomplete or inaccurate.
evidence.quote: Out of the 24 question-response pairs, seven (29.2%) of them had a mean inter-grader score of 3 or less.

evidence.title: A Qualitative Evaluation of ChatGPT4 and PaLM2's Response to Patient's Questions Regarding Age-Related Macular Degeneration
evidence.outcome: Consensus alignment and completeness of LLM answers to AMD patient questions, rated by ophthalmologists
evidence.effect: ChatGPT4 scored 5 from both reviewers on 88.72% for C1 (consensus) and 91.73% for C6 (missing content); PaLM2 on 60.90% and 69.92%.
evidence.quote: Out of 133 questions, ChatGPT4 received a score of five from both reviewers to 118 questions (88.72%) for C1, to 130 (97.74%) for C2, to 131 (98.50%) for C3, to 133 (100%) for C4, to 132 (99.25%) for C5, and to 122 (91.73%) for C6, while PaLM2 to 81 questions (60.90%) for C1, to 114 (85.71%) for C2, to 115 (86.47%) for C3, to 124 (93.23%) for C4, to 113 (84.97%) for C5, and to 93 (69.92%) for C6.

evidence.title: Large language models' responses to liver cancer surveillance, diagnosis, and management questions: accuracy, reliability, readability
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and reliability of chatbot answers to hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis and management questions
evidence.effect: Accurate: ChatGPT 9/20 (45%), Gemini 12/20 (60%), Bing 6/20 (30%); accurate and reliable: 6 (30%), 8 (40%), 3 (15%); no significant accuracy differences
evidence.quote: Of the twenty questions, ChatGPT answered nine (45%), Gemini answered 12 (60%), and Bing answered six (30%) questions accurately; however, only six (30%), eight (40%), and three (15%), respectively, were both accurate and reliable.
evidence.sample_unit: responses (20 questions in triplicate per chatbot)

evidence.title: ChatGPT and retinal disease: a cross-sectional study on AI comprehension of clinical guidelines
evidence.venue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT responses with AAO PPP guidelines, rated by specialists on 1-5 Likert scale
evidence.effect: Overall average score 4.9/5.0, high alignment with AAO PPP guidelines; lowest in surgical management; errors in diagnostic criteria, treatment options, and methodological procedures.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT achieved an overall average score of 4.9/5.0, suggesting high alignment with the AAO PPP guidelines.

evidence.title: Evaluating accuracy and reproducibility of ChatGPT responses to patient-based questions in Ophthalmology: An observational study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT answers to patient ophthalmology questions graded by ophthalmologists
evidence.effect: ChatGPT provided "comprehensive" responses to 70/117 (59.8%) of questions; described as moderate accuracy.
evidence.quote: Totally, 117 questions were inputted into ChatGPT, which provided "comprehensive" responses to 70/117 (59.8%) of questions.

evidence.title: The evaluation of the performance of ChatGPT in the management of labor analgesia
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated safety, accuracy, completeness of ChatGPT4 responses to labor analgesia scenarios
evidence.effect: Deemed safe in 73% of responses (27% unsafe); none unanimously safe across seven experts; accuracy 4/5 (partly accurate); completeness 3.5/5 (somewhat incomplete).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT4 was deemed safe in 73% of responses to the presented obstetric anesthesia clinical scenarios (27% of responses were deemed unsafe).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (each rated by 7 expert obstetric anesthesiologists)

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT 3.5 and 4 as a tool for patient support before and after DBS surgery for Parkinson's disease
evidence.venue: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and harmfulness of LLM answers to DBS questions for Parkinson's disease, graded by specialists
evidence.effect: Correct responses 57.5% (GPT 3.5) and 83.8% (GPT 4); GPT 3.5 gave potentially harmful answers in 6.3% (5/80); no GPT 4 responses were harmful.
evidence.quote: The proportion of responses graded as correct was 57.5% and 83.8% for GPT 3.5 and GPT 4, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (40 questions in English and Portuguese, each answered by GPT 3.5 and GPT 4)

evidence.title: The doc versus the bot: A pilot study to assess the quality and accuracy of physician and chatbot responses to clinical questions in gynecologic oncology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of chatbot answers to gynecologic oncology clinical questions versus physicians
evidence.effect: Physicians gave accurate responses 86.7% vs ChatGPT 60% and Bard 43% (p<0.001 for both); mean quality 4.2 vs 3.0 and 2.8 out of 5.
evidence.quote: Physicians provided a higher proportion of accurate responses (86.7 %) compared to ChatGPT (60 %) and Bard (43 %; p < 0.001 for both).
evidence.sample_unit: response evaluations (10 questions x 3 responders, rated by 3 reviewers)

evidence.title: "Dr. AI Will See You Now": How Do ChatGPT-4 Treatment Recommendations Align With Orthopaedic Clinical Practice Guidelines?
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-4 treatment recommendations with AAOS clinical practice guidelines
evidence.effect: 90% (90 of 100) concordant with AAOS CPGs; 78% (78 of 100) concordant with attending plan; 100% for fracture and hip/knee arthritis, 3 of 10 discordant for carpal tunnel syndrome.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 provided treatment recommendations in accordance with the AAOS CPGs in 90% (90 of 100) of clinical vignettes.

evidence.title: Quality and Accountability of ChatGPT in Health Care in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Simulated Patient Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT diagnoses and medications, and unnecessary or harmful medications, in simulated patient cases
evidence.effect: Correct diagnoses 20/27 (74%); correct medication prescriptions 22/27 (82%); unnecessary or harmful medications 23/27 (85%) even with correct diagnoses.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT had a high level of accuracy in both correct diagnoses (20/27, 74%) and medication prescriptions (22/27, 82%) but a concerning level of unnecessary or harmful medications (23/27, 85%) even with correct diagnoses.
evidence.country: Low- and middle-income countries (not further specified)

evidence.title: Unlocking the potential of advanced large language models in medication review and reconciliation: A proof-of-concept investigation
evidence.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
evidence.outcome: Detection of clinically important drug-drug interactions by LLMs
evidence.effect: All four LLMs recognized warfarin interactions but missed the metoprolol-verapamil interaction; major patient-safety impact was noted for drug interaction identification.
evidence.quote: In terms of potential drug-drug interactions, all LLMs recognized interactions with warfarin but missed the interaction between metoprolol and verapamil.

evidence.title: Unveiling the risks of ChatGPT in diagnostic surgical pathology
evidence.venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
evidence.outcome: Usefulness and error count of ChatGPT diagnostic answers to pathology scenarios
evidence.effect: Useful in 62.2% of cases; only 32.1% of outputs had no errors, the rest had at least one error (894 evaluations).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT provided useful answers in 62.2% of cases, and 32.1% of outputs contained no errors, while the remaining had at least one error.

evidence.title: Lumbar Radicular Pain in the Eyes of Artificial Intelligence: Can You 'Imagine' What I 'Feel'?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4o lumbar radicular pain patterns versus specialist markings
evidence.effect: ChatGPT markings differed significantly from two specialists' markings for L4, L5, and S1 (P < 0.001); ChatGPT lacks capacity to accurately represent LRP patterns.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT currently lacks the capacity to accurately and consistently represent LRP patterns.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated pain pattern markings (L4, L5, S1) at two time points, compared with two specialists' markings

evidence.title: Analysis of ChatGPT Responses to Ophthalmic Cases: Can ChatGPT Think like an Ophthalmologist?
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT primary diagnosis accuracy on ophthalmic cases; hallucination of non-user-provided data
evidence.effect: ChatGPT correctly identified the primary diagnosis in 15 of 17 (88.2%) cases; two cases excluded due to hallucinations or fabrications of nonuser-provided data.
evidence.quote: Overall, ChatGPT correctly identified the primary diagnosis in 15 of 17 (88.2%) cases.

evidence.title: Assessing the performance of large language models (LLMs) in answering medical questions regarding breast cancer in the Chinese context
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to breast cancer treatment questions against oncologist scoring
evidence.effect: Accuracy of the three models on breast cancer treatment questions was lowest, averaging 44.4%; overall about 57-67% comprehensive answers per model.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of the three models in answering questions regarding breast cancer treatment was the lowest, with an average of 44.4%.

evidence.title: Empowering patients: how accurate and readable are large language models in renal cancer education
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and guideline adherence of LLM kidney cancer answers rated by urologists on 5-point scale
evidence.effect: Overall high accuracy (ChatGPT 1.5, Gemini 1.9, Perplexity 2.2) with minor omissions; treatment least accurate (Perplexity 3.1); Gemini gave an answer not adhering to guidelines.
evidence.quote: Gemini AI, for example, provided answers that did not fully adhere to official guidelines, such as stating “A biopsy is the only definitive way to diagnose kidney cancer.”
evidence.sample_unit: patient questions on kidney cancer, each answered by 3 chatbots and rated by 4 urologists

evidence.title: Suitability of ChatGPT as a Source of Patient Information for Screening Mammography
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT breast screening content versus BreastScreen NSW gold standard
evidence.effect: GPT3.5 lacked accuracy, omitting key insights; GPT4 was superior but still included several key omissions.
evidence.quote: GPT4 was deemed superior to GPT3.5 but included several key omissions: PEMAT-P understandability 75.0% (SD = 17) and actionability 53.3% (SD = 11.54); CDC Index 66.0% (SD = 4.1).

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT reliably answer the most common patient questions regarding total shoulder arthroplasty?
evidence.venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
evidence.outcome: Currency and accuracy of ChatGPT clinical knowledge on shoulder arthroplasty questions, graded by surgeons
evidence.effect: Overall grade B-; the chatbot neglected recent research, resulting in recommendations that warrant professional clarification; errors when supplementing its own responses.
evidence.quote: However, the chatbot neglected recent research in its responses, resulting in recommendations that warrant professional clarification.

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT in providing patient information about upper tract urothelial carcinoma
evidence.outcome: Urologist ratings of ChatGPT answers' compliance with EAU guidelines and safety for UTUC questions
evidence.effect: Average overall score 3.93; treatment category lowest (mean 3.68); safety mean 4.02, but a few urologists graded some answers 1 or 2 for safety.
evidence.quote: However, a few urologists considered several answers as unsafe for the patient, by grading them 1 or 2 in this criterion.

evidence.title: ChatGPT for Addressing Patient-centered Frequently Asked Questions in Glaucoma Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated factuality and comprehensiveness of ChatGPT-3.5 glaucoma FAQ answers
evidence.effect: Median scores 4; comprehensiveness lowest (mean 3.7 ± 0.9), factuality 3.9 ± 0.9; 17 (42.5%) questions below 4 for factuality and 24 (60%) for comprehensiveness.
evidence.quote: Comprehensiveness had the lowest scores across domains (mean 3.7 ± 0.9), followed by factuality (mean 3.9 ± 0.9) and coherency and safety (mean 4.1 ± 0.8 for both).

evidence.title: Appropriateness and readability of Google Bard and ChatGPT-3.5 generated responses for surgical treatment of glaucoma
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of LLM glaucoma surgical answers graded by glaucoma specialists
evidence.effect: Appropriate answers in 68% of Google Bard responses and 96% of ChatGPT-3.5 responses.
evidence.quote: Appropriate answers to the posed questions were obtained in 68% of the responses with Google Bard and 96% with ChatGPT-3.5.

evidence.title: Probing clarity: AI-generated simplified breast imaging reports for enhanced patient comprehension powered by ChatGPT-4o
evidence.outcome: Factual accuracy, completeness, and potential harm of simplified reports by BI-RADS category, rated by radiologists
evidence.effect: High factual accuracy (median 2), completeness (median 2), low harm (median 5); BI-RADS 0, 1, 2 reports accurately explained, while BI-RADS 3-6 reports were challenging.
evidence.quote: BI-RADS 0, 1, and 2 reports were accurately explained, while BI-RADS 3-6 reports were challenging.

evidence.title: Qualitatively Assessing ChatGPT Responses to Frequently Asked Questions Regarding Sexually Transmitted Diseases
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, clarity, and appropriateness of ChatGPT answers to STD FAQs on 4-point scale
evidence.effect: 4 of 10 responses excellent requiring no clarification, 6 requiring minimal clarification; no responses graded unsatisfactory.
evidence.quote: Of the responses provided by ChatGPT, 4 were determined to be excellent requiring no clarification and 6 requiring minimal clarification.

evidence.title: Assessing the Clinical Appropriateness and Practical Utility of ChatGPT as an Educational Resource for Patients Considering Minimally Invasive Spine Surgery
evidence.outcome: Clinical appropriateness of ChatGPT responses to MISS FAQs rated by neurosurgeons
evidence.effect: Preoperative and postoperative questions generally appropriate; 50% of intraoperative/technical questions yielded inappropriate or unreliable responses, esp. radiation exposure and lasers.
evidence.quote: Although preoperative and postoperative questions generally elicited clinically appropriate responses, 50% of intraoperative/technical questions yielded either "inappropriate" or "unreliable" responses, particularly for inquiries about radiation exposure and the use of lasers in MISS.

evidence.title: Let's Have a Chat: How Well Does an Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Answer Clinical Infectious Diseases Pharmacotherapy Questions?
evidence.outcome: SME-rated usefulness, correctness, completeness and safety of GPT-3.5 answers to ID pharmacotherapy questions
evidence.effect: 41.8% of responses useful; median (IQR) correctness 7 (4-9), completeness 5 (3-8), safety 8 (4-10).
evidence.quote: Responses were mostly considered correct and safe but were often incomplete, suggesting that GPT-3.5 responses may not replace an ID pharmacist's responses.

evidence.title: Generation of preoperative anaesthetic plans by ChatGPT-4.0: a mixed-method study
evidence.outcome: Clinical appropriateness of LLM-generated anaesthetic plans versus consultants and adjudication committee
evidence.effect: Plans showed variable agreement with consultants; inappropriate recommendations included subpar postoperative pain management and failure to recommend tracheal intubation for patients at high risk of aspiration.
evidence.quote: While some differences were not deemed clinically significant, subpar postoperative pain management advice and failure to recommend tracheal intubation for patients at high risk for pulmonary aspiration were considered inappropriate recommendations.

evidence.title: Assessing the quality of AI information from ChatGPT regarding oral surgery, preventive dentistry, and oral cancer: An exploration study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT dental answers, including diagnostic methods and post-operative instructions
evidence.effect: Preventive dentistry scored 4.3/5; oral surgery 3.9/5 and oral cancer 3.6/5, with gaps in post-operative instructions, personalized risk assessments, and specialized diagnostic methods.
evidence.quote: While achieving the highest score for preventive dentistry at 4.3/5 and being able to communicate the complex information coherently, the tool showed lower accuracy for oral surgery and oral cancer, scoring 3.9/5 and 3.6/5, respectively, with several gaps for post-operative instructions, personalized risk assessments, and specialized diagnostic methods.

evidence.title: ChatGPT's Attitude, Knowledge, and Clinical Application in Geriatrics Practice and Education: Exploratory Observational Study
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT identification of drug-drug and drug-disease interactions in polypharmacy vignette
evidence.effect: Identified 7 common PIMs, 5 drug-drug and 3 drug-disease interactions; missed 5 drug-disease and 1 drug-drug interaction; 2 hallucinations.
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT missed 5 drug-disease and 1 drug-drug interaction and produced 2 hallucinations.

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a GPT4-Based Orofacial Pain Clinical Decision Support System
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of GPT4 primary and differential diagnoses against gold-standard diagnoses
evidence.effect: Overall diagnostic score was 157/300 (52%); differential diagnoses were accurate in 80% of cases (400/500 points).
evidence.quote: The model provided accurate differential diagnoses in 80% of cases (400 out of 500 points).
evidence.sample_unit: anonymized orofacial pain patient case descriptions

evidence.title: Proficiency, Clarity, and Objectivity of Large Language Models Versus Specialists' Knowledge on COVID-19's Impacts in Pregnancy: Cross-Sectional Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on COVID-19 and pregnancy clinical knowledge questionnaire
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 and Copilot 97% (32/33), Bard 94% (31/33), ChatGPT-3.5 82% (27/33); ChatGPT-4 incorrectly stated increased miscarriage risk; minor inaccuracies for Bard and Copilot.
evidence.quote: In terms of LLMs' knowledge, ChatGPT-4 and Microsoft Copilot each scored 97% (32/33), Google Bard 94% (31/33), and ChatGPT-3.5 82% (27/33).

evidence.title: Quantitative evaluation of GPT-4's performance on US and Chinese osteoarthritis treatment guideline interpretation and orthopaedic case consultation
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 accuracy and completeness interpreting AAOS and Chinese osteoarthritis guidelines
evidence.effect: Correct match rate 46.4%; accuracy score 4.3±1.6 (95% CI 3.9 to 4.7); completeness 2.8±0.6; complete agreement with all score-2 recommendations.
evidence.quote: In interpreting the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons and Chinese OA guidelines, GPT-4 achieved a correct match rate of 46.4% and complete agreement with all score-2 recommendations.

evidence.title: Are AI chatbots concordant with evidence-based cancer screening recommendations?
evidence.outcome: Concordance of AI clinical knowledge with current USPSTF screening guidelines
evidence.effect: 43 of 60 (71.7%) criteria completely concordant, 3 (5%) moderately concordant, 14 (23.3%) not concordant or not present; 9 of 14 non-concordant from oldest age group prompts.
evidence.quote: 43 of 60 (71.7 %) criteria were completely concordant, 3 (5 %) were moderately concordant and 14 (23.3 %) were not concordant or not present, with most of the non-concordant criteria (9 of 14, 64.3 %) being from prompts for the oldest age groups.
