evidence.title: Assessing online chat-based artificial intelligence models for weight loss recommendation appropriateness and bias in the presence of guideline incongruence
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness and completeness of chatbot obesity treatment answers versus ADA/AACE guidelines
evidence.effect: All Copilot and 8/10 Gemini responses appropriate; none inappropriate. Copilot complete 10/10 versus Gemini 5/10.
evidence.quote: Microsoft Copilot (10/10; 100%) provided a higher proportion of complete responses than Google Gemini (5/10; 50%).

evidence.title: Assessing the performance of AI chatbots in answering patients' common questions about low back pain
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of chatbot low back pain recommendations against clinical guidelines
evidence.effect: Of 120 responses yielding 1069 recommendations, 55.8% were accurate, 42.1% inaccurate and 1.9% unclear.
evidence.quote: Out of 120 responses yielding 1069 recommendations, 55.8% were accurate, 42.1% inaccurate and 1.9% unclear.

evidence.title: Exploring potential drug-drug interactions in discharge prescriptions: ChatGPT's effectiveness in assessing those interactions
evidence.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT drug-interaction knowledge (occurrence, severity, onset) versus Micromedex reference
evidence.effect: Occurrence identified 100%; severity accuracy 37.3%; onset accuracy 65.2%, with limits in documentation prediction.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.0 accurately identified pDDIs (100 % for occurrence) but had limited accuracy for severity (37.3 %) and moderate accuracy for onset (65.2 %).

evidence.title: Evaluating the utility of ChatGPT in enhancing parental education and clinical support in hypospadias care
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT responses on hypospadias diagnosis, treatment, and postoperative care
evidence.effect: 41% of responses completely accurate, 35% accurate but inadequate, 24% inaccurate; Fleiss' Kappa 0.607 among six pediatric urologists.
evidence.quote: In the qualitative assessment, 41 % of responses were deemed completely accurate, with 35 % considered accurate but inadequate, and 24 % rated as inaccurate.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Performance of Three Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Comparative Study Based on Actual Cases
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnosis, differential diagnosis, examination and treatment quality scored by experts on real cases
evidence.effect: Med-Go median 37.5 (IQR 31.9-41.5), Gemini 33.0 (IQR 25.5-36.6), p<0.001; differential diagnosis weakest, treatment strongest; inaccuracies could lead to adverse decisions.
evidence.quote: Analysis revealed that responses related to differential diagnosis were the weakest, while those pertaining to treatment recommendations were the strongest.

evidence.title: A Review of ChatGPT as a Reliable Source of Scientific Information Regarding Endodontic Local Anesthesia
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT answers with peer-reviewed evidence-based literature on endodontic anesthesia
evidence.effect: ChatGPT matched literature-based responses in 16 of 32 questions (50% reliable).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT was reliable 50% of the time when compared to the peer-reviewed, evidence-based literature.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language model performance to support the diagnosis and management of patients with primary immune disorders
evidence.venue: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical reasoning quality (R-IDEA) of LLMs on rare primary immune disorder vignettes
evidence.effect: Three models had accuracy >88% and R-IDEA ≥8 (GPT-4o 96.2%); the other three had accuracy near 60% or lower and R-IDEA ≤0.55 (Mistral-7B 42.3%).
evidence.quote: Conversely, the remaining 3 models fell below acceptable accuracy rates near 60% or lower and had poor R-IDEA scores (≤0.55), with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 attaining the worst diagnostic accuracy (42.3%).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence in neurovascular decision-making: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4 and multidisciplinary expert recommendations for unruptured intracranial aneurysms
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 treatment recommendation quality and congruence with neurovascular board decisions
evidence.effect: No factual hallucinations; no specific recommendation derivable in 25% of cases; median expert quality rating 3.4/5; congruent with board in 65% of cases; moderate to low interrater agreement.
evidence.quote: None of the recommendations generated reflected evidence of factual hallucination, although in 25% of the case studies no specific recommendation could be derived from the GPT-4 responses.
evidence.sample_unit: patients with unruptured intracranial aneurysms (case scenarios)

evidence.title: Evaluating Adherence to Canadian Radiology Guidelines for Incidental Hepatobiliary Findings Using RAG-Enabled LLMs
evidence.venue: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
evidence.outcome: adherence to current guidelines
evidence.effect: Adherence was 81.7% and 79.3% without RAG, and 97.2% and 95.1% with RAG.
evidence.quote: Adherence rates were 81.7% for GPT-4o without RAG, 97.2% for GPT-4o with RAG, 79.3% for o1-mini without RAG, and 95.1% for o1-mini with RAG.

evidence.title: Use of large language models as clinical decision support tools for management pancreatic adenocarcinoma using National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with current NCCN guideline-based clinical scenarios
evidence.effect: 35% of ChatGPT and 42% of Copilot responses missing information; 14% and 25% inaccurate/misleading respectively.
evidence.quote: Copilot responses were completely correct in 33% (n = 17) of responses, whereas 42% (n = 22) were missing information and 25% (n = 13) contained inaccurate/misleading information.

evidence.title: Comparing AAOS appropriate use criteria with ChatGPT-4o recommendations on treating distal radius fractures
evidence.outcome: Agreement between ChatGPT-4o and AAOS appropriate use criteria for distal radius fracture treatments
evidence.effect: Agreement ranged from 99.17% (immobilization without reduction) and 90.42% (volar locking plates) to 15% (dorsal plating); mean error ranged 0.6 to -2.9; ChatGPT-4o favored conservative approaches.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o does not consistently align with the appropriate use criteria in determining appropriate management of distal radius fractures.
evidence.sample_unit: paired treatment appropriateness scores (240 patient scenarios)

evidence.title: ChatGPT Performance on 120 Interdisciplinary Allergology Questions-Systematic Evaluation With Clinical Error Impact Assessment for Critical Erroneous AI-Guided Chatbot Advice
evidence.venue: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
evidence.outcome: Clinical accuracy errors, including critical errors, in ChatGPT allergology answers
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 4.1/5 (SD 0.78); six critical errors (1 dermatology, 2 pediatrics, 3 pulmonology); a pediatric food allergen error was potentially life-threatening.
evidence.quote: Six critical errors were identified: 1 in dermatology, 2 in pediatrics, and 3 in pulmonology.

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT be trusted as a resource for a scholarly article on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT literature-based answers on implant treatment planning versus best available evidence
evidence.effect: ChatGPT's original answers to all six questions were revised after higher-quality, timely studies were supplied, and the revisions often reversed the original conclusions (e.g., splinting, cantilevers, overdenture preference).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT has not demonstrated the ability to accurately cull the literature, stratify the rigor of the evidence, and extract accurate implications from the studies selected to deliver the best evidence-based answers to questions on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses.

evidence.title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: LLM application of deprescribing criteria to patient cases, error types
evidence.effect: Errors due to complex inclusion/exclusion criteria (54.5%) and ambiguous clinical contexts such as missing information (39.3%); step 2 PPV 0.47, F1 0.58.
evidence.quote: Adjudication revealed that while the model excelled at identifying when there was a deprescribing criterion related to one of the patient's medications, it often struggled with determining whether that criterion applied to the specific case due to complex inclusion and exclusion criteria (54.5% of errors) and ambiguous clinical contexts (eg, missing information; 39.3% of errors).

evidence.title: AI in clinical decision-making: ChatGPT-4 vs. Llama2 for otolaryngology cases
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and appropriateness of recommended examinations and treatment versus expert decisions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 diagnosed 82% correctly vs Llama2 76%; appropriate tests 88% vs 83%; appropriate treatment 80% vs 72%; both sometimes suggested inappropriate tests.
evidence.quote: Sometimes, both systems suggested inappropriate tests.

evidence.title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Knowledge gaps causing missed serious condition
evidence.effect: Global-search RAG missed an emergency drug-interaction message, likely because the knowledge graph lacked COVID-19 drug-drug interaction resources.
evidence.quote: This misclassification likely occurred due to the absence of specific COVID-19 drug-drug interaction resources in the knowledge graph.

evidence.title: Comparison of ChatGPT's Diagnostic and Management Accuracy of Foot and Ankle Bone-Related Pathologies to Orthopaedic Surgeons
evidence.venue: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
evidence.outcome: Completeness of ChatGPT-4 clinical knowledge and treatment options for foot and ankle bone pathologies
evidence.effect: Average score 4.53/5 per criterion and 22.7/25 per case; lowest for hallux rigidus (21.3). Comprehensive information beyond standard treatment options was limited.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT struggled to provide comprehensive information beyond standard treatment options.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4 for addressing patient-centred frequently asked questions in age-related macular degeneration clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated factuality and comprehensiveness of ChatGPT-4 AMD answers; outdated technologies noted
evidence.effect: 23 (62%) of 37 questions had mean comprehensiveness below 4 and 21 (57%) had factuality below 4; comments flagged superseded or older technologies and techniques not routinely used in practice.
evidence.quote: Free-text comments highlighted issues related to superseded or older technologies, and techniques that are not routinely used in clinical practice, such as genetic testing.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Cardiovascular Antithrombotic Care: Performance, Accuracy, and Implications for Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on validated cardiovascular antithrombotic care scenarios
evidence.effect: Claude 3 Opus answered 85% correctly; GPT-4o 55%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 44%, GPT-3.5 10%. Some free-tier models gave inappropriate medical advice to clinicians.
evidence.quote: The performance of LLMs in cardiovascular clinical scenarios varied widely, with some models outperforming clinicians, and some free-tier models providing inappropriate medical advice to clinicians.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Performance and Safety of Large Language Models in Generating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Plans: A Comparative Study With Physicians Using Real Patient Records
evidence.outcome: Completeness and necessity of medications in GPT-4 plans versus guideline-based reference plan
evidence.effect: Physicians' plans had fewer missing medications than GPT-4 (p=0.008). GPT-4 plans included fewer unnecessary medications (p=0.003). Dosage accuracy (p=0.975) and overall error scores (p=0.301) did not differ.
evidence.quote: Results indicated that physicians' management plans had fewer missing medications compared to those generated by GPT-4 (p=0.008).

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence perspective on geriatric syndromes: assessing the information accuracy and readability of ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Geriatrician-rated accuracy of ChatGPT answers against current guidelines (0-4 scale)
evidence.effect: Overall mean accuracy 88% (3.52/4); lowest for sarcopenia diagnosis (2.0) and depression treatment (2.5).
evidence.quote: Responses generated for sarcopenia diagnosis and depression treatment in older adults had the lowest accuracy scores (2.0 and 2.5, respectively).
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT responses to FAQs about geriatric syndromes

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT's adherence to EULAR diagnostic criteria and therapeutic protocols for rheumatoid arthritis at two distinct time points, 14 days apart, utilizing binary and multiple-choice inquiries
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT clinical knowledge against EULAR RA guideline-based questions
evidence.effect: 86% (43/50 multiple-choice items) correct at baseline and 84% (42/50) on day 14. Some errors persisted, so knowledge was largely but not fully guideline-concordant.
evidence.quote: At baseline, 43 (86%) of the multiple-choice items were answered correctly.

evidence.title: Precision Oncology in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer: A Comparative Study of Contextualized ChatGPT Models
evidence.outcome: Recommendation of guideline non-concordant therapies by base GPT models
evidence.effect: Base GPT-4 gave non-concordant therapies in 4/12 responses and GPT-4o in 5/12; PDF+Prompt model had none.
evidence.quote: No PDF+Prompt model responses contained guideline non-concordant therapies in contrast to 4/12 responses for GPT4 (P = 0.093) and 5/12 responses for GPT4o (P = 0.037).

evidence.title: Opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence in patient portal messaging in primary care
evidence.outcome: Outdated clinical knowledge and omission of serious diagnoses in AI drafts
evidence.effect: AI drafts contained outdated COVID vaccine timing advice and omitted DKA and blood clot urgency; 4 of 18 drafts (22%) erroneous.
evidence.quote: Four (22%) of these PPMs were identified as erroneous.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4o-Generated Exercise Plans for Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus-Assessment of Their Safety and Other Quality Criteria by Coaching Experts
evidence.outcome: Safety of AI exercise plans vs ADA/ACSM guidelines, including contraindications and medical check-up advice
evidence.effect: Most common safety gap was missing advice for medical check-up (rated low in 8 of 9 plans); high-intensity training recommended for a patient with proliferative retinopathy; safety instructions incomplete.
evidence.quote: High-intensity training was recommended for Patient 3 with proliferative retinopathy.

evidence.title: Assessing the quality and readability of ChatGPT responses to frequently asked questions about trigger finger release
evidence.venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT clinical answers about trigger finger release on four-point scale
evidence.effect: Average accuracy score 1.9 (between excellent and satisfactory); one incorrect response and occasional factual inaccuracies, particularly treatment recommendations.
evidence.quote: Although the chatbot provided largely accurate information, it produced an incorrect response in one case and displayed occasional factual inaccuracies, particularly regarding treatment recommendations.

evidence.title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and a Paediatric Intensive Care Specialist in Responding to Medical Education Questions: A Multicenter Evaluation
evidence.venue: Journal of paediatrics and child health
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated completeness and accuracy of ChatGPT-4 vs PICU specialist answers on factual and reasoning questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 preferred in 60% of factual comparisons (p<0.001) and more complete (p=0.02); specialist preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons, ChatGPT-4 less accurate (p<0.0001).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated superior completeness in factual knowledge (p = 0.02) but lower accuracy in clinical reasoning (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Performance of a virtual assistant based on ChatGPT-4 in the diagnosis of syndromes with orofacial manifestations
evidence.venue: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy, completeness, and up-to-dateness of differential diagnoses and recommended exams
evidence.effect: Correct diagnosis identified in 96.2% of cases (80.8% first hypothesis); completeness and up-to-dateness scored lowest; failed to mention all diagnostic steps in 7.69% of cases.
evidence.quote: Despite the high accuracy rate, the assistant failed to mention all diagnostic steps in 7.69% of the cases.

evidence.title: Challenging cases of hyponatremia incorrectly interpreted by ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Whether ChatGPT-3.5 recognized the crucial cause of hyponatremia and gave adequate therapy in four difficult cases
evidence.effect: In 2023 ChatGPT missed the crucial cause in all four cases, as did the 46 clinicians. In 2024 it diagnosed and managed one case adequately. It recognized Addison's disease in case 1, which 81% of clinicians missed.
evidence.quote: Neither ChatGPT, in 2023, nor the previously published assessment by 46 clinicians, whose assessment was described in the original publication, recognized the most crucial cause of hyponatremia with major therapeutic consequences in all four cases.
evidence.sample_unit: published challenging hyponatremia cases (each submitted twice, Dec 2023 and Sep 2024)
evidence.country: Multiple (Canada, Netherlands, South Africa, Taiwan, USA)

evidence.title: Enhancing responses from large language models with role-playing prompts: a comparative study on answering frequently asked questions about total knee arthroplasty
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Clinical knowledge accuracy and completeness of LLM answers versus established guidelines
evidence.effect: Gemini overstated topical medications and arthroscopy for OA, contradicting guidelines; Claude erred on implants and preoperative antibiotics; Q7 and Q9 responses all unacceptable for missing probabilistic data or surgical details.
evidence.quote: For instance, Google Gemini overstated the effectiveness of topical medications and the role of arthroscopic surgery in osteoarthritis management, contradicting established guidelines.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (10 questions x 4 models x 2 prompt types)

evidence.title: Enhancing patient-centered care with AI: a study of responses to neuroendocrine neoplasms queries
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy, clarity and completeness of LLM answers to neuroendocrine neoplasm management questions
evidence.effect: Mean scores: ChatGPT Plus 3.72, Copilot 3.54, Perplexity 3.22, with clarity rated highest; the chemotherapy indications question scored lowest.
evidence.quote: The chemotherapy indications question received the lowest scores, underscoring LLM challenges in handling complex clinical decisions.
evidence.sample_unit: raters (22 expert physicians and 24 NEN patients) scoring responses to 9 questions

evidence.title: Effectiveness of ChatGPT for Clinical Scenario Generation: A Qualitative Study
evidence.outcome: Expert-panel review of GPT-4 cardiovascular scenarios for clinical accuracy and guideline adherence
evidence.effect: All five experts found the scenarios realistic and guideline-consistent, but they also documented specific errors, incorrect recommendations, missing information, and inconsistencies with standard nursing practice.
evidence.quote: All the experts agreed that the scenarios were realistic and followed clinical guidelines.

evidence.title: Human-AI collectives most accurately diagnose clinical vignettes
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
evidence.outcome: Whether LLM differential diagnoses omitted the correct diagnosis
evidence.effect: LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all in 34% to 54% of cases depending on the LLM; individual physicians often supplied the missed diagnosis, frequently ranking it first.
evidence.quote: Crucially, when LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all (range across LLMs: 34% to 54%; Right -most columns), individual humans did mention it in a substantial number of cases (range across LLMs: 30% to 38%; Right -most columns excluding Bottom - Right cells), most frequently ranking it first (range across LLMs: 20% to 26%, Top - Right cells).
evidence.sample_unit: text-based medical case vignettes (40,762 physician differential diagnoses)

evidence.title: Assessing Accuracy of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer's Responses to Common Patient Questions Regarding Congenital Upper Limb Differences
evidence.venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT clinical answers on congenital hand differences, graded by surgeons
evidence.effect: Of 164 grades, 83 (51%) needed no clarification, 37 (23%) minimal, 32 (20%) moderate, 13 (8%) unsatisfactory; considerable variability in depth; omitted that syndromic involvement is rare.
evidence.quote: In total, 164 grades were assigned to the 82 ChatGPT responses: 83 (51%) did not require any clarification, 37 (23%) required minimal clarification, 32 (20%) required moderate clarification, and 13 (8%) received an unsatisfactory rating.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (16 FAQs plus 2 psychosocial questions, each queried multiple times)

evidence.title: Appropriateness of acute breast symptom recommendations provided by ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Adherence of LLM breast symptom advice to ACR guidelines and clinical judgment, rated by breast radiologists
evidence.effect: Appropriate for 7/7 (100%) common symptom questions, but only 3/9 (33%) pregnancy-associated breast symptom questions and 3/4 (75%) palpable abnormality management/imaging questions.
evidence.quote: In contrast, ChatGPT-3.5 generated responses were appropriate for 3/9 (33 %) questions about pregnancy-associated breast symptoms and 3/4 (75 %) questions about management and imaging recommendations for a palpable breast abnormality.

evidence.title: The role of generative artificial intelligence in deciding fusion treatment of lumbar degeneration: a comparative analysis and narrative review
evidence.venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with 2014 JNS lumbar fusion guidelines
evidence.effect: Concordance 66.67% ChatGPT 4o, 58.33% Perplexity, 54.17% Gemini, 50% Copilot; non-concordant answers were insufficient or over-conclusive (Copilot 37.5% over-conclusive).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT 4o had the highest concordance rate at 66.67%, with non-concordant responses distributed at 16.67% for both insufficient and over-conclusive classifications.

evidence.title: An assessment of generative artificial intelligence in responding to clinical queries on tapering antidepressants
evidence.venue: Research in social & administrative pharmacy : RSAP
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of tapering recommendations against guidelines
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy, completeness, and clarity compared less favourably; the hyperbolic tapering response was inaccurate, referring to logarithmic reductions and giving incorrect fixed dosage reduction examples.
evidence.quote: This was due to inaccuracies as the response incorrectly referred to logarithmic reductions and provided inaccurate examples of fixed dosage reductions.

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models' ability to identify clinically relevant drug-drug interactions and generate high-quality clinical pharmacotherapy recommendations
evidence.venue: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
evidence.outcome: Quality and safety of LLM DDI management recommendations versus ground truth
evidence.effect: GPT-4 recommendations optimal in 8/13 (61.5%) cases (P=0.05 vs ground truth); two GPT-4 and one Gemini 1.5 recommendation deemed to result in potential patient harm.
evidence.quote: Two recommendations from GPT-4 and one recommendation from Gemini 1.5 were deemed to result in potential patient harm.
evidence.sample_unit: patient cases (vignettes) with a drug-drug interaction

evidence.title: Retrieval-augmented generation elevates local LLM quality in radiology contrast media consultation
evidence.outcome: contraindication recommendations
evidence.effect: Base Llama had 8% hallucinations, particularly in contraindication recommendations; RAG eliminated them (0%).
evidence.quote: Qualitative assessment by a radiologist revealed that hallucinations—particularly in contrast dosing and contraindication recommendations—were present in 8% of responses from the base Llama model and were eliminated (0%) in the RAG-enhanced version (χ²₍Yates₎ = 6.38, p = 0.012; Fisher p = 0.0068).

evidence.title: The potential utility of CHATGPT4.0 as an AI assistant in the education and management of patients with Barrett's esophagus
evidence.venue: Diseases of the esophagus : official journal of the International Society for Diseases of the Esophagus
evidence.outcome: Gastroenterologist-rated accuracy of ChatGPT responses on Barrett's esophagus questions
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 4.01 out of 5; 79.3% of responses completely accurate or mostly accurate with minor errors, implying about one fifth had greater inaccuracies.
evidence.quote: Gastroenterologists rated ChatGPT responses as mostly accurate overall (4.01 out of 5) with 79.3% of responses completely accurate or mostly accurate with minor errors.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Readability of ChatGPT in Addressing Patient Queries on Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery
evidence.outcome: Surgeon-rated accuracy of ChatGPT answers to patient questions on spinal deformity surgery
evidence.effect: 59.7% excellent, 26.3% satisfactory, 12.3% moderate clarification needed, 1.8% unsatisfactory; one response (pain return/worsening) rated inaccurate by all reviewers.
evidence.quote: 59.7% of responses were excellent (no clarification needed), 26.3% were satisfactory (minimal clarification needed), 12.3% required moderate clarification, and 1.8% were unsatisfactory, with one response ("Will my pain return or worsen?") rated inaccurate by all reviewers.

evidence.title: ChatGPT Performance Deteriorated in Patients with Comorbidities When Providing Cardiological Therapeutic Consultations
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated appropriateness of drug recommendations and contraindicated drug recommendations in high-risk scenarios
evidence.effect: Approval 86.90% GPT-4 vs 85.06% GPT-3.5 (p=0.0476); error patterns differed (p<0.001); GPT-4 more often recommended contraindicated drugs in high-risk scenarios.
evidence.quote: notably, GPT-4 more frequently recommended contraindicated drugs in high-risk scenarios.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenarios (each prompted 10 times per model)

evidence.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Facial Injection Planning: Comparative Performance and Safety Limitations
evidence.outcome: Chatbot treatment plan safety, product selection, and injection strategy ratings on Likert scales
evidence.effect: ChatGPTo1 and ChatGPT4o scored higher than Claude, CopilotPro, and Llama (p<0.05); ChatGPTo1 safety score 1.30 ± 0.17; total scores 7.87 and 7.85 of 10; safety limitations remain.
evidence.quote: However, safety limitations remain and preclude unsupervised clinical use.

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and LLaMA for reliability, quality, and accuracy in familial Mediterranean fever
evidence.outcome: LLM answer alignment with SHARE/EULAR FMF guidelines
evidence.effect: LLaMA fully aligned on 51.6% (16/31), ChatGPT 80.6% (25/31); 9.7% (4/31) of LLaMA responses entirely contradictory to guidelines, none for ChatGPT.
evidence.quote: While 9.7% (4/31) of LLaMA's responses were entirely contradictory to the guidelines, ChatGPT did not produce any such responses.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Generative Artificial Intelligence Systems in Solving Clinical Pharmacy Problems: Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Omission of critical contraindications and guideline currency in LLM pharmacy answers
evidence.effect: 75% of models omitted critical contraindications (eg, ethambutol in optic neuritis); 90% erroneously recommended macrolides for drug-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae; only DeepSeek-R1 aligned with updated AAP guidelines for pediatric doxycycline.
evidence.quote: Critical limitations were observed across models, including high-risk decision errors-75% omitted critical contraindications (eg, ethambutol in optic neuritis) and a lack of localization-90% erroneously recommended macrolides for drug-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (China's high-resistance setting), while only DeepSeek-R1 aligned with updated American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) guidelines for pediatric doxycycline.

evidence.title: To Self-Treat or Not to Self-Treat: Evaluating the Diagnostic, Advisory and Referral Effectiveness of ChatGPT Responses to the Most Common Musculoskeletal Disorders
evidence.outcome: Expert Likert ratings of diagnosis, recommendation, and referral accuracy of ChatGPT responses
evidence.effect: Most responses rated adequate or excellent; diagnosis scores differed by area of interest (p = 0.007), attributed to trauma-related questions; no significant difference in other categories.
evidence.quote: However, in the diagnosis category, a significant difference was found in the evaluation made according to the AoI (p = 0.007), which is attributed to trauma-related questions.

evidence.title: Evaluation of performance of generative large language models for stroke care
evidence.outcome: LLM stroke care accuracy versus clinical guidelines, rated by clinicians against 60-point threshold
evidence.effect: Most scores fell below the 60 competency threshold; treatment stage scores 48.2-57.8; gains typically only 60-65 at most.
evidence.quote: Most scores fell below the minimum clinical competency threshold of 60, and even when LLMs exceeded this benchmark, the gains were marginal, typically only reaching 60 to 65 at most.

evidence.title: Are clinical improvements in large language models a reality? Longitudinal comparisons of ChatGPT models and DeepSeek-R1 for psychiatric assessments and interventions
evidence.venue: The International journal of social psychiatry
evidence.outcome: Adherence of pharmacological recommendations to established guidelines and diagnostic completeness
evidence.effect: Pharmacological recommendations frequently diverged from established guidelines; primary diagnoses broadly accurate but often omitted somatic factors and comorbidities.
evidence.quote: Pharmacological recommendations frequently diverged from established guidelines, whilst cultural adaptations remained largely superficial.

evidence.title: Performance of Microsoft Copilot in the Diagnostic Process of Pulmonary Embolism
evidence.venue: The western journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: Inclusion of PE in differential diagnosis and sensitivity of high-risk categorization
evidence.effect: PE was in top-10 differential in 94.3% of cases; sensitivity for high-risk category was 34%, specificity 97.1%, NPV 59.6%.
evidence.quote: Copilot correctly included PE in the differential diagnosis in 94.3% of cases by listing it within the top 10 conditions.

evidence.title: Accuracy and Safety of ChatGPT-3.5 in Assessing Over-the-Counter Medication Use During Pregnancy: A Descriptive Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Correctness, completeness, safety of ChatGPT-3.5 OTC pregnancy answers versus UpToDate
evidence.effect: Median correctness 5 (IQR 5-5), completeness 4 (IQR 4-5), safety 5 (IQR 5-5); safety errors in 9% of evaluations (n=8), including omissions risking serious complications.
evidence.quote: Despite high overall scores, the safety errors in 9% of the evaluations (n = 8), including omissions that pose a risk of serious complications, currently renders the chatbot an unsafe standalone resource for this purpose.

evidence.title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT status epilepticus recommendations' adherence to NCS/AES/EFNS guidelines and completeness
evidence.effect: Rarely recommended side positioning (25%) and neurological assessment (0-25%); dosing lacking when unprompted; non-established therapies suggested; GPT-5 not higher adherence than GPT-4o.
evidence.quote: However, it rarely recommended key measures such as side positioning (25%) to prevent potential aspiration and neurological assessments (0-25%).

evidence.title: The Impact of Access to Clinical Guidelines on LLM-Based Treatment Recommendations for Chronic Hepatitis B
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: Currency of LLM clinical knowledge versus current guidelines
evidence.effect: GPT-4 without external context gave outdated treatment recommendations for chronic hepatitis B; coherence was 51%, and errors persisted (91%) even with context.
evidence.quote: Consequently, this setup allowed us to specifically isolate and demonstrate the impact of providing access to an up‐to‐date external document, effectively showcasing GPT‐4's vulnerability to providing outdated or incorrect treatment recommendations without immediate contextualisation.

evidence.title: Evaluating Medium Scale, Open-Source Large Language Models: Towards Decision Support in a Precision Oncology Care Delivery Context
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Outdated, incomplete, or factually incorrect clinical content in LLM answers to oncology questions
evidence.effect: A large percentage of answers contained outdated or incomplete information as well as factual errors; overall performance was modest.
evidence.quote: Our findings identified significant issues, where a large percentage of answers contained outdated or incomplete information, as well as factual errors.

evidence.title: Comparison of Artificial Intelligence Models and Human Experts in Managing Dyslipidemia: Assessment of Adherence to Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy versus ESC/EAS guidelines, including LDL-C targets and risk stratification
evidence.effect: AI correct 91.0% (Claude 94.3%, GPT-4 90.7%, DeepSeek 87.9%); 25 errors, 56% risk miscalculation, 8.0% wrong LDL-C target; DeepSeek weaker in risk assessment (2.3 vs 2.9).
evidence.quote: AI models achieved guideline compliance in 382 out of 420 responses (91.0%), significantly exceeding all human groups.

evidence.title: The imitation game: large language models versus multidisciplinary tumor boards: benchmarking AI against 21 sarcoma centers from the ring trial
evidence.venue: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM sarcoma treatment recommendations with guideline-based expert MTB recommendations and harmful alternatives
evidence.effect: Common human recommendations often absent in LLM outputs; best model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) aligned with experts in only 60% of cases; potentially harmful alternative recommendations observed.
evidence.quote: Discrepancies were particularly notable, where common human recommendations were often absent in LLM outputs.
evidence.sample_unit: anonymized soft tissue sarcoma cases (each queried 21 times per model)

evidence.title: From Guidelines to Real-Time Conversation: Expert-Validated Retrieval-Augmented and Fine-Tuned GPT-4 for Hepatitis C Management
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: Baseline GPT-4 accuracy on guideline-based HCV knowledge and treatment selection
evidence.effect: Baseline binary accuracy 36.6% (guideline authors), 50% (tertiary experts); baseline correct DAA regimen in only 24% of scenarios.
evidence.quote: The baseline model demonstrated a median accuracy of 24.0% (IQR: 22%), the RAG-Top1 configuration showed marked improvement with a median accuracy of 58.0% (IQR: 10%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001), the RAG-Top10 configuration emerged as the superior performer, achieving a median accuracy of 76.0% (IQR: 8%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001) and the SFT model demonstrated a median accuracy of 66.0% (IQR: 19%, vs. baseline, p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: queries (15 open-ended questions and 25 simulated clinical scenarios)

evidence.title: Large language model processing capabilities of ChatGPT 4.0 to generate molecular tumor board recommendations-a critical evaluation on real world data
evidence.outcome: Level of evidence of LLM therapy recommendations versus human MTB
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 4.0 occasionally used lower-level or preclinical evidence more frequently than hMTB (P = .0019); information density similar (0.67 vs 0.75; P = .084).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT 4.0 occasionally utilized lower-level or preclinical evidence more frequently (P = .0019).

evidence.title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence-based patient education models for irritable bowel syndrome
evidence.venue: Indian journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Indian Society of Gastroenterology
evidence.outcome: Comprehensiveness and accuracy of LLM answers to IBS FAQs, including outdated content
evidence.effect: Gemini comprehensive and accurate for 94.9% (37/39), ChatGPT 89.7% (35/39); mixed responses were vague or outdated; no significant difference (p = 0.67).
evidence.quote: Gemini produced comprehensive and accurate answers for 94.9% (37/39) of questions, with two rated as mixed (vague/outdated).

evidence.title: ChatGPT and low back pain - Evaluating AI-driven patient education in the context of interventional pain medicine
evidence.outcome: Completeness and correctness of ChatGPT low back pain answers against guideline-based grading
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 2.81/3; under 6% fully incorrect; 18–30% partially correct, mostly omission of key safety considerations.
evidence.quote: A substantial portion (18–30 %, depending on prompt) were rated as partially correct (score = 2), typically due to omission of key safety considerations or incomplete diagnostic explanations.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (25 questions x 6 prompt conditions x 3 reviewers' consensus)

evidence.title: Automated production of comparison tables for shared decision making: Comparing a human-generated table (Option Grid), a search engine process, and outputs from four large language models
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM-generated clinical content versus expert Option Grid
evidence.effect: Accuracy was 97% for the ChatGPT models and OpenBioLLM-70b and 95% for OpenBioLLM-8b and the Google search process; several tables omitted alternative interventions.
evidence.quote: Accuracy, compared to the human Option Grid, was 97 % for the ChatGPT models and the open-source OpenBioLLM-70b, and 95 % for OpenBioLLM-8b and the Google search process.
evidence.sample_unit: comparison tables (one human Option Grid, four LLM tables, one Google search table)

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4's performance on pediatric dentistry questions: accuracy and completeness analysis
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT-4 pediatric dentistry answers by topic
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 4.21 for FAQs and 4.16 for curricular questions; accuracy varied by topic (p=0.007), highest for fissure sealants (4.45), lowest for pulpal therapy (3.93).
evidence.quote: Accuracy scores for curricular questions varied significantly by topic (p = 0.007), with the highest score for fissure sealants (4.45 ± 0.62; median: 5) and the lowest for pulpal therapy (3.93 ± 0.93; median: 4).

evidence.title: Concordance of an Artificial Intelligence Model (ChatGPT 4.0) with Physician Decisions in Smoking Cessation Clinics: A Comparative Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT-4.0 smoking cessation treatment recommendations versus physician decisions, by case complexity
evidence.effect: Overall concordance 67.1%; 32.9% inappropriate. Inappropriate recommendations in 81.5% of chronic disease cases and 77.8% of regular medication cases (p=0.021, p=0.030).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.0 provided inappropriate recommendations in 81.5% of cases involving chronic diseases and 77.8% of cases involving regular medication use (p = 0.021, p = 0.030, respectively).

evidence.title: Evaluating the performance of ChatGPT in clinical multidisciplinary treatment: a retrospective study
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT etiology reasoning and diagnostic accuracy in complex MDT cases versus physicians
evidence.effect: ChatGPT median overall score 41.0/50 vs MDT physicians 43.5 (p = 0.001); lower accuracy (p < 0.001); higher comprehensiveness (p < 0.001); lacked ability to reason through etiologies of complex cases.
evidence.quote: Analysis of specific questions revealed that ChatGPT lacked the ability to reason through the etiologies of complex cases.

evidence.title: Can large language models follow guidelines? A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek AI in clavicle fracture management based on AAOS recommendations
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to guideline-based clavicle fracture questions, rated by orthopedic surgeons
evidence.effect: Binary accuracy ChatGPT 0.93 vs DeepSeek 0.89; weighted accuracy 0.83 vs 0.79 (p > 0.05); occasional inaccuracies and hallucinations observed.
evidence.quote: Both models demonstrated generally high accuracy levels.

evidence.title: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4 Plus in Providing Information on Oral Cancer Management
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT-4 Plus answers to oral cancer diagnosis, treatment, recovery, prevention questions
evidence.effect: 63% of 65 responses were Score 1, none Score 4. Score 1 was 72% in Recovery, 62% Treatment, 60% Prevention, 55% Diagnosis. Scores 2 and 3 were highest in Diagnosis (45%). ICC 0.85 to 0.93.
evidence.quote: Among 65 questions, 63% of responses were Score 1, with none rated as Score 4.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Nutrition: A Descriptive Comparison of ChatGPT- and Dietitian-Planned Diets for Chronic Disease Scenarios
evidence.venue: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
evidence.outcome: Safety and nutritional adequacy of ChatGPT diet plans versus dietitian plans, including contraindicated foods
evidence.effect: ChatGPT diets had notable deficiencies in meeting energy and nutrient requirements, lacked personalization, and in several cases included contraindicated foods.
evidence.quote: In several cases, contraindicated foods were included.

evidence.title: Evaluating AI-Generated Meal Plans for Simulated Diabetes Profiles: A Guideline-Based Comparison of Three Language Models
evidence.venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM dietary plans with T2DM guidelines and the nutrition care process
evidence.effect: None of the models fully matched the NCP framework, particularly diagnosis and monitoring. Energy alignment was 70.9% for ChatGPT-4.1 and 83.1% for Grok-3. There were fat overestimation, micronutrient shortfalls, and carbohydrate underdelivery.
evidence.quote: None of the models demonstrated full concordance with the NCP framework, particularly in the diagnosis and monitoring components.

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language model-generated medical information on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF guidelines (0-4 scale)
evidence.effect: Gemini higher than ChatGPT-4: median 3.0 [3.0-3.5] vs 3.0 [2.5-3.0], p=0.0029; neither model fully concordant with guidelines.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, neither model provided answers in full concordance with established clinical guidelines, and their readability remained a major challenge.

evidence.title: Can Chatbots Please Both Patients and Experts? Benchmarking AI and Clinical Guidelines for Hearing Loss
evidence.venue: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
evidence.outcome: Chatbot answer accuracy against hearing loss clinical practice guidelines, rated by otolaryngologists
evidence.effect: Best chatbots fully guideline-concordant for up to 50% of questions; earlier models 25% to 37.5%. Misleading content was rare and typically not clinically significant.
evidence.quote: The most advanced chatbots achieved full guideline-concordant accuracy for up to 50% of questions, while earlier models ranged from 25% to 37.5%.

evidence.title: The ABCs of PEMs: Using Artificial Intelligence to Enhance the Readability of Patient Educational Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics
evidence.venue: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of AI-generated pediatric orthopaedic PEMs rated by blinded surgeons
evidence.effect: Total accuracy: OrthoInfo 6.95, ChatGPT 6.15, OpenEvidence 3.25; total completeness: OrthoInfo 6.98, ChatGPT 5.90, OpenEvidence 3.05.
evidence.quote: OrthoInfo PEMs were rated highest for accuracy and completeness (total accuracy: 6.95; total completeness: 6.98), compared to Chat GPT (total accuracy: 6.15; total completeness: 5.90) and Open Evidence (total accuracy: 3.25; total completeness: 3.05), but ChatGPT approached OrthoInfo in several subdomains, including treatment descriptions, timeline, and follow-up recommendations.

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
evidence.outcome: Clinical knowledge errors and incomplete differentials in LLM infection control recommendations, qualitatively reviewed
evidence.effect: Critical deficiencies in all models: DeepSeek V3 recommended TB treatment without considering NTM; GPT-4.1 wrongly advised against single-room isolation for MDRA; wrong C. auris screening sites.
evidence.quote: These findings, summarized in Table 6 , reveal that even the higher-performing models may generate clinically significant and potentially unsafe recommendations.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical infection control scenarios (165 outputs rated by 16 experts)

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models in Analyzing Common Hypertension Scenarios
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, safety, and guideline concordance of LLM hypertension management recommendations versus expert
evidence.effect: GPT-4 accuracy 83%, safety 86% vs expert 92%/93%; Gemini 64%/73%; MedLM 35%/39%. Guideline-concordant: GPT-4 46%, Gemini 35%, MedLM 14%, expert 68%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 had the highest accuracy (83%) and safety (86%) scores among LLMs but remained inferior to expert responses (92% accuracy, 93% safety).

evidence.title: Appraisal of ChatGPT's responses to common patient questions regarding acromioclavicular joint dislocations
evidence.outcome: Surgeon-graded accuracy of ChatGPT clinical answers on 5-point Likert scale, by question category
evidence.effect: Average score 4/5 (good quality with minor inaccuracies); treatment questions scored lower than rehabilitation (P = .025).
evidence.quote: Treatment-related questions scored lower compared to other categories, with a significant difference observed between treatment and rehabilitation (P = .025).

evidence.title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
evidence.outcome: Concordance of AI treatment recommendations with expert consensus and guidelines, discordant cases
evidence.effect: TSB recommended endocrine therapy for three low ER-positive DCIS cases where MTB withheld; also recommended redundant genetic testing and RT without considering margin status in two patients.
evidence.quote: Similarly, TSB automatically recommended RT after lumpectomy in two patients without considering margin status or the need for re-excision.

evidence.title: Using artificial intelligence models to generate dietary recommendations for chronic kidney disease patients: A comparative cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: AI dietary advice conformity to KDIGO 2024 guideline; missed contraindications
evidence.effect: Models overlooked contraindications (low-protein diet in severe hypoalbuminemia), neglected age-specific needs, and lacked real-time knowledge updates. Accuracy scores 6.875-7.25, not significantly different (p=0.715).
evidence.quote: The AI models share several common limitations: they might overlook contraindications (such as recommending a low-protein diet for patients with severe hypoalbuminemia), neglect age-specific needs, and lack real-time knowledge updates.

evidence.title: Feasibility analysis of generative artificial intelligence tools as a means of medical science popularization on urological diseases
evidence.outcome: Inaccurate, outdated or oversimplified clinical knowledge in ChatGPT content
evidence.effect: Evaluators found 54 unreasonable contents, including 25 inaccurate knowledge (11 errors, 6 outdated knowledge, 8 overly simple descriptions) and 29 unclear logic.
evidence.quote: Two evaluators evaluated the content of ChatGPT 4.0 and found 54 unreasonable contents, including inaccurate knowledge (25 in total, 11 of errors, 6 of outdated knowledge, 8 of overly simple description) and unclear logic (29 in total, 13 of repeated content, 16 of inconsistent content with the topic) ( Table 2 ).
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated content items (8 diseases x 4 aspects)

evidence.title: Large language model as a clinical decision support tool in the initial management of critically ill children: a pilot evaluation
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness, harm, and omissions of LLM diagnostic vs therapeutic recommendations in pediatric critical care
evidence.effect: Diagnostic recommendations appropriate 94% (ED) and 98% (PICU); therapeutic only 82%. Potentially harmful therapeutic suggestions 7% vs 2% (ED) and 10% vs 0% (PICU); 0.95 critically missing therapeutic recommendations per PICU case.
evidence.quote: Potentially harmful therapeutic suggestions were more common than diagnostic ones: 7% vs. 2% in the ED (p = 0.016) and 10% vs. 0% in the PICU (p < 0.00001).

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Dietary Advice to Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome: ChatGPT vs. Google Gemini
evidence.venue: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
evidence.outcome: Compliance of LLM dietary responses with IBS clinical guidelines (Guideline Compliance Score)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 70% and Gemini 57.5% of responses guideline-compliant; no significant difference between models (p > 0.05), so a substantial share of responses were noncompliant.
evidence.quote: This study found that most responses from ChatGPT (70%) and Gemini (57.5%) were compliant with the guidelines, but there was no significant difference in guideline compliance, quality, understandability, actionability, or readability scores (p > 0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses to IBS dietary questions

evidence.title: Can Large Language Models Draft Safe, Reliable Patient Leaflets on Driving After Stroke in Comparison to the Stroke Association Leaflet?
evidence.outcome: Factual accuracy/misinformation of leaflet content on driving after stroke
evidence.effect: Stroke Association leaflet had perfect factual accuracy; Copilot and DeepSeek showed occasional omissions in seizure and TIA guidance.
evidence.quote: The Stroke Association leaflet achieved perfect factual accuracy and referencing, whereas Microsoft Copilot and DeepSeek demonstrated occasional omissions in seizure and transient ischemic attack (TIA) guidance.
evidence.sample_unit: patient information leaflets (7 LLM-generated, 1 Stroke Association)

evidence.title: Evaluating Generative AI Large Language Models for Urticaria Management: A Comparative Analysis of DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4o
evidence.outcome: Errors in LLM urticaria answers compared against clinical guidelines
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 answers contained no errors versus guidelines, while ChatGPT-4o made errors in three clinical questions.
evidence.quote: When compared with the guidelines, the answers provided by DeepSeek-R1 contained no errors, while ChatGPT-4o made errors in three clinical questions.

evidence.title: Accuracy of artificial intelligence in carpal tunnel syndrome management: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro
evidence.outcome: LLM treatment appropriateness ratings versus AAOS guideline ratings for carpal tunnel syndrome scenarios
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o under-recommended steroid injection (-2.7) and carpal tunnel release (-1.8), over-recommended electrodiagnostic studies (+4.5); Gemini similar pattern; Spearman Rho 0.782 (Gemini) vs 0.53 (ChatGPT)
evidence.quote: Compared to AAOS guidelines, ChatGPT-4o under-recommended steroid injection (mean error -2.7 ± 1.2; P < .001) and carpal tunnel release (mean error -1.8 ± 1.7; P < .001) while over-recommending electrodiagnostic studies (mean error 4.5 ± 3.8; P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: paired treatment ratings across 135 patient scenarios

evidence.title: Comparing guideline adherence and readability: Artificial intelligence with deep learning versus specialized physicians in peripheral artery disease management
evidence.outcome: LLM adherence to 2024 ACC/AHA PAD guideline versus physicians, scored by three experts
evidence.effect: Adherence did not differ (physicians median 5.8 vs LLMs 7.3, p=0.169); CoT-LLMs highest (9.7). LLMs more often recommended supervised exercise (84.6% vs 30.0%) and revascularization for quality of life (69.2% vs 20.0%).
evidence.quote: LLM showed comparable guideline adherence to physicians although CoT models achieved the highest scores.
evidence.sample_unit: responses (30 physician, 13 LLM system) to a standardized PAD case

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o as a Patient Information Tool for Common Orthopaedic Surgeries: Accuracy, Completeness, and Clinical Utility
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM clinical content on orthopaedic procedures, incl. risks and alternatives
evidence.effect: Factual accuracy >90%, but 36% of responses contained misleading or incomplete information; surgical risk responses performed worst; mean DISCERN 43.5 (fair).
evidence.quote: Factual accuracy was high (>90%), but 36% of responses contained some misleading or incomplete information.

evidence.title: Accuracy, Readability, Understandability, and Actionability of ChatGPT Responses to Patient Questions on Systemic Isotretinoin Treatment
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-3.5 responses on isotretinoin, including outdated information
evidence.effect: Of 90 evaluations, 44.4% comprehensive and correct, 18.8% correct but insufficient, 32.2% mixed with outdated data, 4.4% completely incorrect.
evidence.quote: Of the 90 evaluations, 44.4% of responses were comprehensive and correct, 18.8% were correct but insufficient, 32.2% were mixed with outdated data, and 4.4% were completely incorrect.
evidence.sample_unit: rater evaluations of ChatGPT responses (30 questions x 3 raters)

evidence.title: AI for evidence-based treatment recommendation in oncology: a blinded evaluation of large language models and agentic workflows
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and comprehensiveness of LLM treatment recommendations against current evidence (June 2024 cutoff)
evidence.effect: Comprehensiveness was low for general LLMs (29.3-36.0%) and Myelo (32.7%), and accuracy 48.0-64.7% for general LLMs; HopeAI 74.0% comprehensiveness.
evidence.quote: HopeAI demonstrated superior performance across accuracy (82.0%), relevance (85.3%), and comprehensiveness (74.0%), compared to OpenAI o1-preview (64.7, 57.3, 36.0%), Claude 3.5 Sonnet (50.0, 51.3, 29.3%), Gemini 1.5 Pro (48.0, 46.0, 30.0%), and Myelo (58.7, 56, 32.7%).

evidence.title: Benchmarking GPT-5 in radiation oncology: measurable gains, but persistent need for expert oversight
evidence.outcome: Hallucinations and clinical knowledge errors in GPT-5 radiation oncology treatment plans
evidence.effect: Hallucinations flagged in 10.0% of individual reviewer assessments (24 of 240); no case reached majority consensus; substantive errors persisted, clustered in complex scenarios needing precise trial knowledge.
evidence.quote: Hallucinations were rare, flagged in 10.0% of all individual reviewer assessments (24 of 240), and no patient case reached majority consensus for their presence.
evidence.sample_unit: radiation oncology vignettes (plus 300 TXIT multiple-choice items)

evidence.title: Are Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer Answers to Patient Questions Regarding Fecal Incontinence Accurate, Complete, and Consistent With the American Society of Colorectal Surgeons Clinical Practice Guidelines?
evidence.venue: Diseases of the colon and rectum
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, completeness, and guideline consistency of ChatGPT answers on fecal incontinence
evidence.effect: No version was entirely accurate, complete, or guideline-consistent; accuracy 61% (3.5), 72% (4), 50% (5 Free), 83% (5 Plus); most frequent error theme was inaccurate treatment recommendations.
evidence.quote: No version of Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer provided answers that were entirely accurate, complete, or consistent with clinical practice guidelines; however, the paid version performed markedly better than the other versions.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (each presented twice to four ChatGPT versions)

evidence.title: AI vs. MD: Benchmarking ChatGPT and Gemini for Complex Wound Management
evidence.outcome: Agreement of LLM wound management recommendations with expert consensus, including contraindications
evidence.effect: Perfect agreement in management recommendations was 75.0% for Gemini vs 60.0% for ChatGPT; both models wrongly suggested NPWT in a case potentially contraindicated by severe infection.
evidence.quote: Gemini achieved a slightly higher percentage of perfect agreement in management recommendations (75.0% vs. 60.0% for ChatGPT).

evidence.title: Large Language Models in Patient Health Communication for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Pilot Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis
evidence.outcome: LLM answers to ASCVD treatment questions aligned with latest clinical guidelines
evidence.effect: None of the models consistently provided responses aligned with latest guidelines for the standard ASCVD treatment regimen; performance weaker for treatment and prevention than definitions and diagnosis.
evidence.quote: Specifically, none of the models consistently provided responses aligned with the latest clinical guidelines for the following key guideline-facing question "What is the standard treatment regimen for ASCVD?"

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of six large language models in perioperative decision support for geriatric patients with multimorbidity: a three-dimensional evaluation framework
evidence.outcome: Guideline compliance and completeness of perioperative recommendations, including omissions of protocols
evidence.effect: NYAAI omitted temperature management and delirium protocols; general-purpose models showed moderate guideline compliance (ChatGPT 4/5; Gemini 3/5) but produced contextually inappropriate recommendations.
evidence.quote: However, it exhibited selective guideline adherence, omitting temperature management and delirium protocols.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated clinical case (scored outputs from six LLMs)

evidence.title: Dosage adjustments in renal impairment among medical ward patients: ChatGPT® and DeepSeek® models' effectiveness in assessing those adjustments
evidence.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
evidence.outcome: AI clinical knowledge on renal dosing compared with current guideline (UpToDate)
evidence.effect: Accuracy 61.7% for ChatGPT 5.0 and 67.5% for DeepThink against UpToDate; modest improvement across ChatGPT versions.
evidence.quote: With advances in the ChatGPT® model, there was a modest improvement in prediction capacity, with the latest ChatGPT® 5.0 achieving balanced performance (64.3 % sensitivity, 54.8 % specificity, 61.7 % accuracy).
evidence.sample_unit: prompts (drug orders requiring renal dose adjustment)

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Understanding of Perianal Fistula MRI Findings Using ChatGPT: A Randomized, Single Centre Study
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate and unverified recommendations in GPT-4o MRI fistula report summaries
evidence.effect: Hallucinations occurred in 11% of 250 outputs, with unverified recommendations also identified.
evidence.quote: In Phase II, hallucinations occurred in 11% of outputs, with unverified recommendations also identified.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Show Comparable Response Performance but Vary in Readability Regarding Patient Questions on Hip Arthroscopy
evidence.outcome: Expert-graded accuracy and incorrect response rate of LLM answers on hip arthroscopy
evidence.effect: Mean Likert grades 3.0 (ChatGPT), 2.9 (Microsoft), 2.6 (Gemini), P=.481; overall incorrect response rate among LLMs was 20%.
evidence.quote: The overall incorrect response rate among LLMs was 20%.

evidence.title: A comparative study on DeepSeek and ChatGPT for bone and soft tissue tumor clinical practice
evidence.outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy on sarcoma diagnosis, imaging, pathology, staging, and treatment questions
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 74.7% (DeepSeek) and 55.4% (ChatGPT); both models shared 51 errors, indicating gaps in clinical knowledge.
evidence.quote: Cross-model analysis revealed DeepSeek uniquely answered 60 questions correctly where ChatGPT erred, while both models shared 51 errors.

evidence.title: Assessing Generative AI Chatbots for Alcohol Misuse Support: A Longitudinal Simulation Study
evidence.outcome: Clinician-rated quality of information and inappropriate or inaccurate guidance in chatbot responses
evidence.effect: Quality of information was the lowest-rated domain (mean 2.7/5). Every chatbot had one or more examples of inappropriate, over-stated, or inaccurate guidance.
evidence.quote: Across all chatbots, empathy was the highest-rated domain (mean score 4.6/5) while quality of information was the lowest (mean 2.7/5).

evidence.title: AI-Generated Antibiotic Therapies for Acute Periprosthetic Joint Infections with Implant Retention in Comparison with an Interdisciplinary Team
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI antibiotic recommendations with interdisciplinary team, and therapy duration
evidence.effect: Agreement 0-33% in multidrug-resistant/complex cases; up to 57% (95% CI 0.47-0.67) in monomicrobial cases; AI consistently recommended 12 weeks vs 6 weeks by the team.
evidence.quote: Notably, in cases involving multidrug-resistant organisms and more complex clinical scenarios, the AI-generated recommendations were incongruent with those of the IT, with estimated percentage agreement ranging from 0-33%.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM management recommendations with AAOS 2022 and AAP 2016 guidelines
evidence.effect: Concordant scenarios: guided 20/20 (100%) correct, non-logged-in 19/20 (95%). Mismatch scenarios: guided 3/10 correct, non-logged-in 6/10 correct.
evidence.quote: Guided ChatGPT: Achieved 100% accuracy.

evidence.title: Can AI generate safe anaesthesia plans? A comparative evaluation of three large language models on 100 synthetic cases
evidence.outcome: LLM preoperative anaesthetic plan conformity to French guidelines, expert-scored 0-4 across 12 domains
evidence.effect: ChatGPT highest conformity, 98% completeness, highest median in 7 of 12 domains; Dougall GPT moderate; Mistral lowest conformity and highest proportion of unsafe or potentially unsafe outputs (scores ≤2).
evidence.quote: Dougall GPT performed moderately, whereas Mistral LeChat showed lower conformity and the highest proportion of unsafe or potentially unsafe outputs (scores ≤2).

evidence.title: Evaluating the Clinical Decision-Making Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence in Common Geriatric Syndromes Using Evidence-Based Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Completeness and guideline alignment of ChatGPT clinical responses to geriatric vignettes, including omissions
evidence.effect: Completeness 55/70, accuracy 59/70, guideline alignment 61/70; reviewers identified key omissions such as missing assessments or guideline-recommended tools in multiple vignettes; urinary incontinence scored lowest.
evidence.quote: Reviewers identified key omissions, such as missing assessments or guideline-recommended tools, in multiple vignettes.
evidence.sample_unit: standardized geriatric vignettes (each rated by 5 geriatricians)

evidence.title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM differential/diagnosis selection for emergent chest pain conditions
evidence.effect: Baseline over-called emergent conditions (specificity 45.2%); with prevalence cues or no categories, sensitivity fell to 30.4% and 8.8%, missing emergent diagnoses.
evidence.quote: With baseline prompting, GPT-4o systematically over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%); adding prevalence cues or removing diagnostic category constraints respectively increased specificity (83.0% and 94.7%) while reducing false alarms by 107 and 140 per 500, but at the cost of poor sensitivity (30.4% and 8.8%).

evidence.title: Patient perspective on large-language model responses to questions about Moyamoya
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated omission of recent advances and research in LLM answers
evidence.effect: Answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%).
evidence.quote: Physicians evaluating the same LLM outputs reported the answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%) and failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).
evidence.sample_unit: community respondent survey sets (27 ChatGPT, 20 Gemini)

evidence.title: Evaluating large language model responses to patient questions on ulnar collateral ligament repair
evidence.outcome: Surgeon-rated accuracy of LLM answers to UCL repair patient questions (CRRS, AIRM)
evidence.effect: More than minimal clarification needed for 15% ChatGPT, 5% Gemini, 40% Grok responses; Gemini CRRS 1.5±0.5 vs ChatGPT 2.0±0.4 and Grok 2.1±0.7.
evidence.quote: More than minimal clarification was required for 15% (3/20) of ChatGPT, 5% (1/20) of Gemini, and 40% (8/20) of Grok responses.
evidence.sample_unit: patient questions (responses from each of 3 models)

evidence.title: When AI joins the table: evaluating large language model performance in soft tissue sarcoma tumor board decisions
evidence.venue: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated ChatGPT-4o tumor board recommendation quality across five domains versus maximum score
evidence.effect: Scores were significantly lower than the maximum of 1.0 across all five criteria (all p < 0.0001); discrepancies in treatment sequencing and chemotherapy selection.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o scores were significantly lower than the maximum achievable value of 1.0 across all five criteria (all p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Will AI keep you out of trouble? An expert panel review of LLMs for hazardous regional anesthesia consults
evidence.outcome: Detection of hazardous regional anesthesia scenarios by LLMs, scored by expert panel
evidence.effect: Gemini detection 75% zero-shot, 84% chain-of-thought; ChatGPT 56% and 50%; CoPilot 32% and 45%; no LLM consistently identified hazards.
evidence.quote: No LLM consistently identified hazardous scenarios for regional anesthesiology contained in the prompts to a review panel consensus standard with either prompting method.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (20 hazardous prompts x 3 LLMs x 2 prompting strategies)

evidence.title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
evidence.outcome: standard-of-care and emergency-response errors
evidence.effect: F-ACAD had 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns about US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and communication.
evidence.quote: Although F-ACAD reviewed more sources and produced a more complex algorithm, its own AI critics identified 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns related to US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and parent-friendly communication.
evidence.sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

evidence.title: Opportunities and Challenges of Visual Large Language Models in Imaging Diagnostics: Lessons from Brain Metastasis Detection in Clinical MRI
evidence.outcome: Specificity and hallucinated lesions in vLLM brain metastasis MRI reports
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 100% for both; specificity GPT-4o 8%, Sonnet 3.5 4%; accuracy 54% and 52%; both models hallucinated additional lesions in 12% of cases.
evidence.quote: Both models hallucinated additional lesions in 12% of cases.

evidence.title: Safety and user perception of general-purpose large language models in pediatric healthcare: Evaluations of ChatGPT by doctors and parents
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT answers to pediatric health questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT3.5: 73.2% correct or correct-but-not-comprehensive, 26.8% partially or completely incorrect; ChatGPT4: 68.3% vs 31.7%; no significant difference between versions (p = .819).
evidence.quote: Experts rated 73.2% of responses from ChatGPT3.5 as "completely correct" or "correct but not comprehensive," while 26.8% were rated as "partially incorrect" or "completely incorrect."

evidence.title: Accuracy, readability, and understandability of European Association of Urology guidelines bot for Sexual and Reproductive Health Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of bot answers to guideline-derived questions, rated by two experts on a 5-point Likert scale
evidence.effect: 224/228 (98.3%) accurate, 2/228 (0.9%) fair, 2/228 (0.9%) not accurate; completeness 223/228 (97.8%) complete; no difference between strong and weak recommendations.
evidence.quote: In terms of accuracy 224/228 (98.3%) were defined as accurate (score-4-5), 2/228 (0.9%) presented a fair accuracy (score = 3) while 2/228 (0.9%) were deemed not accurate (score 1-2).

evidence.title: Effect of Emotional Prompt on the Quality of ChatGPT Based Discharge Instructions After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Using ERAS Derived Benchmarks
evidence.outcome: Completeness of LLM clinical content against ERAS guidelines
evidence.effect: Core domains 100% present, but full antibiotic details only 25.0%, fibre reintroduction 41.7%, adaptation period 30.0%, GI symptom monitoring 33.3%.
evidence.quote: Only 25.0% of outputs addressed full antibiotic prescription details, while specific dietary components (eg, vegetables, fruits, cereals) were each covered in fewer than 25.0% of cases.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated discharge instruction outputs (30 per prompt type)

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models in supporting autoimmune liver disease diagnosis and clinical decision-making: advantages of reasoning-based models
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs on confirmed AILD cases, including overlap syndrome
evidence.effect: o1-preview overall diagnostic accuracy 81.0%; all models showed reduced diagnostic accuracy for AIH-PBC overlap syndrome.
evidence.quote: All models demonstrated reduced diagnostic accuracy for autoimmune hepatitis-primary biliary cholangitis overlap syndrome.

evidence.title: Accuracy and Knowledge Base Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3 in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: an Expert-Rated Blinded Study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated guideline concordance of LLM answers to bariatric surgery questions (0-3 scale)
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-V3 2.44±0.40, ChatGPT-4o 1.79±0.46, Gemini 2.0 Flash 1.63±0.47 (p<0.001); fully concordant (score 3) in 80% DeepSeek vs 0% ChatGPT and 3.3% Gemini.
evidence.quote: Fully guideline-concordant ratings (score = 3) were most frequent for DeepSeek (80%) vs. ChatGPT (0%) and Gemini (3.3%).

evidence.title: Effect of large language model on diagnostic accuracy and clinical completeness among nephrology fellows managing transplant infection
evidence.outcome: Clinically significant hallucination and niche dose-duration knowledge gaps in LLM-aided responses
evidence.effect: Only a single clinically significant hallucination (3.3%) occurred; minimal or no benefit in dual infection scenarios and niche dose-duration knowledge.
evidence.quote: Only a single clinically significant hallucination (3·3%) occurred.

evidence.title: Efficacy of ChatGPT in personalized glucose-lowering strategy development: a clinician-based comparative study
evidence.outcome: Reasonableness of AI glucose-lowering strategies by case complexity, including medication contraindications
evidence.effect: Mean scores fell from 89.90 ± 2.936 (simple, A-level) to 76.12 ± 11.93 (complex, C-level) (p <.0020); ChatGPT-4o 82.24 vs attending physicians 86.35 (p = .0467).
evidence.quote: However, its accuracy in complex cases, especially concerning medication contraindications, requires improvement.

evidence.title: Structural error asymmetry and harm-weighted analysis of ChatGPT versus ICU Physicians in acid-base interpretation: a prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity for mixed acid-base disorders and respiratory component detection
evidence.effect: Mixed-disorder sensitivity 0.96 for ICU physicians vs 0.63 for ChatGPT; respiratory component sensitivity 0.88 vs 1.00.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity for mixed acid–base disorders was 0.96 for ICU physicians and 0.63 for ChatGPT.
evidence.sample_unit: consecutive ICU patients' arterial blood gas interpretations

evidence.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence as a Decision-Support Tool in Urological Tumor Boards: A Study in Real Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT-4o oncologic recommendations with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions
evidence.effect: Full agreement in 56.1% of cases, correct but incomplete in 23.5%, partially accurate but flawed in 18.4%; Cohen's kappa 0.61. Discrepancies most common in metastatic prostate cancer (tumor burden misclassification, treatment sequencing errors).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o fully agreed with the MTB in 56.1% of cases, was correct but incomplete in 23.5%, and provided partially accurate but flawed recommendations in 18.4%.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence diet plans underestimate nutrient intake compared to dietitians in adolescents
evidence.outcome: AI diet plan nutrient content versus dietitian reference and adolescent guidelines
evidence.effect: AI systematically undercalculated energy (bias +695 kcal), protein (+19.9 g), lipid (+15.8 g), carbohydrate (+114.6 g); protein 21.5-23.7% and lipid 41.5-44.5% above guidelines, carbohydrate 32.4-36.3% below.
evidence.quote: AI models have exhibited clinically significant deviations in diet plans for adolescents at both macro and micro levels.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Patient-Centered Periprocedural Anticoagulation in Interventional Radiology
evidence.outcome: LLM concordance with current SIR guidelines for withholding, reinitiation timeframes, platelet and INR thresholds
evidence.effect: Claude, GPT-4o, Mistral withholding ~1.86-1.88/2; reinitiation ~1.34-1.37; LLaMA (0.76) and Qwen (0.52) significantly underperformed across all categories (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: LLaMA (0.76) and Qwen (0.52) significantly underperformed across all categories (p<0.001).

evidence.title: Multidisciplinary expert evaluation of large language models on questions regarding bariatric surgery: a comparative analysis of ERNIE Bot 4.0, ChatGPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini Pro
evidence.outcome: Comprehensiveness and completeness of LLM clinical answers on bariatric surgery
evidence.effect: All LLMs sub-optimal in comprehensiveness: Claude 3 Opus 3.13, Gemini Pro 3.06, ERNIE 2.91, ChatGPT-4 2.86 out of 5.
evidence.quote: All four LLMs performed sub-optimally, but Claude 3 Opus (3.13 ± 0.46) and Gemini Pro (3.06 ± 0.44) outperformed ChatGPT 4.0 (2.86 ± 0.41) and ERNIE Bot 4.0 (2.91 ± 0.48).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses to bariatric surgery questions

evidence.title: Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Comparative Analysis of Chat-GPT and Breast Radiologists on ACR Appropriateness Criteria
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT imaging appropriateness ratings with ACR Appropriateness Criteria
evidence.effect: All ChatGPT versions had significant mean bias vs ACR (GPT-4o 2.463; GPT-4 1.7623; GPT-3.5 2.4691; all p<0.001) versus radiologists 0.2438 (p=0.489).
evidence.quote: All versions of ChatGPT had larger mean biases that were significant (GPT-4o: 2.463; GPT-4: 1.7623, GPT-3.5: 2.4691, all p<0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: imaging decisions rated (10 ACR breast imaging clinical variants)

evidence.title: ChatGPT and patient education in benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, in French and in English
evidence.venue: European annals of otorhinolaryngology, head and neck diseases
evidence.outcome: Alignment of ChatGPT BPPV answers with AAO-HNSF guidelines, graded 1-4 by two otolaryngologists
evidence.effect: 12 of 14 responses fully guideline-aligned (grade 4/4); 2 accurate but lacking detail on fall risk in older persons (grade 3/4); English and French responses uniform.
