evidence.quote: The 2 other responses, although accurate, lacked detail on the risk of falls in older persons with BPPV (grade 3/4).

evidence.title: Large Language Model Performance and Clinical Reasoning Tasks
evidence.outcome: Failure rate of LLMs generating differential diagnoses versus final diagnoses on clinical vignettes
evidence.effect: Failure rates exceeded 0.80 (range, 0.90-1.00) for differential diagnosis in all models; below 0.40 (range, 0.09-0.39) for final diagnosis.
evidence.quote: Failure rates exceeded 0.80 (range, 0.90-1.00) for differential diagnosis in all models but were less than 0.40 (range, 0.09-0.39) for final diagnosis.

evidence.title: Chatbot Responses to Frequently Asked Questions About Cannabis and Its Use for Cancer Symptoms
evidence.venue: Journal of pain and symptom management
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and comprehensiveness of cannabis/cancer symptom answers, including missing adverse effects and drug interactions
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 9.0 (ChatGPT), 8.8 (Gemini), 8.3 (Co-Pilot); comprehensiveness 8.1, 8.5, 7.2. Some inaccurate statements and missing adverse effect and drug interaction information.
evidence.quote: Inaccurate or misleading statements regarding cannabis formulations and symptom benefits were identified, with missing information on adverse effects and drug interactions.

evidence.title: AI Assessment and Management of Visceral Aneurysms Using ChatGPT-4o-mini: A Pilot Study Examining the Feasibility of Automating the AI Validation Process
evidence.outcome: Guideline-based management correctness
evidence.effect: Human evaluators rated 67% correct; AI self-assessed 89% correct (scores 1-2).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o-mini self-assessed 89% of responses as correct (scores 1-2), compared to 67% by human evaluators (chi-square, P < 0.0001), with the greatest discrepancy in the partially correct category.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated visceral aneurysm clinical scenarios and responses

evidence.title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Completeness and urgency of LLM clinical advice on isotretinoin during suspected pregnancy
evidence.effect: LLM responses did not consistently convey the urgency of discontinuing isotretinoin when pregnancy is suspected, nor adequately convey folic acid importance. One response recommended stopping only after a positive pregnancy test.
evidence.quote: However, the LLMs did not consistently recommend immediately stopping isotretinoin or sufficiently guide the patient to take folic acid.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

evidence.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Three Large Language Models for Parent-Centered Questions About Anorexia Nervosa
evidence.venue: The International journal of eating disorders
evidence.outcome: Omission of clinically relevant information and lower accuracy on diagnosis questions
evidence.effect: Omission of clinically relevant information was the most common limitation; accuracy was lower across models for diagnosis and clinical assessment questions. DeepSeek had more factual inaccuracies.
evidence.quote: Qualitative error analysis indicated that the omission of clinically relevant information was the most common limitation, while DeepSeek produced more factual inaccuracies and Gemini more generalized guidance.

evidence.title: Analysis of AI-Generated Radiography Responses Using a Closed-System LLM
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated currency and completeness of Copilot's radiography clinical knowledge
evidence.effect: Experts flagged incomplete or superficial content and outdated terminology and standards, including shielding and grid use, in Copilot responses; no numeric rates reported.
evidence.quote: However, concerns were raised about incomplete or superficial content, attributions outside a radiologic technologist's scope of practice, outdated terminology and standards (including shielding and grid use), lack of specificity, and insufficient clinical context.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (AI responses) reviewed by 7 subject matter experts

evidence.title: Omission and hallucination prevalence of clinical guidelines in diagnostic large language model outputs
evidence.outcome: Omission of clinical guidelines in LLM diagnostic outputs
evidence.effect: Guideline omissions up to 97% for DeepSeek-V3 and 46% for GPT-4.1.
evidence.quote: We analysed a total of 12 197 LLM outputs, which quantifies three hazard areas: omissions (up to 97% for DeepSeek-V3 and 46% for GPT-4.1), hallucinations (up to 9%) and inconsistencies (guideline citation rate ranging from 0% to 78.39% across sociodemographic vignettes).

evidence.title: Decomposing Persona Prompts for Simulated Clinical Reasoning: A Two-by-Two Factorial In Silico Experiment of Time Pressure and Safety Prioritization
evidence.outcome: Differential diagnosis completeness and top-ranked accuracy across prompt conditions
evidence.effect: Gold diagnosis was in the top five in all runs; top-ranked accuracy lowest in high/lean (50/56, 89.3%) versus 100% in safety-first conditions; high time pressure narrowed differential entropy (beta -0.246).
evidence.quote: Top-ranked accuracy was high overall but was lowest in the high/lean condition (50 of 56 runs, 89.3%) (Table 3 ).
evidence.sample_unit: runs (28 synthetic vignettes x 4 personas x 2 repeats)

evidence.title: Open-Source Large Language Models Distilled DeepSeek-R1 Pose Challenges for On-Premises Clinical Deployment in Medical Diagnosis: A Comparative Study of Performance
evidence.outcome: Error modes in chain-of-thought for incorrect diagnostic cases, including diagnostic priority inversion
evidence.effect: Three error modes prevalent across distilled models: reasoning drift, red-flag recognition failure, and diagnostic priority inversion (qualitative; no counts reported).
evidence.quote: Qualitative analysis of the chain-of-thought outputs in incorrect cases revealed three universally prevalent error modes across distilled models: Reasoning drift, Red-Flag recognition failure, and diagnostic priority inversion.

evidence.title: ChatGPT in Public Cardiovascular Healthcare: Accuracy, Limitations, and Implications
evidence.venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Correctness of ChatGPT diagnostic hypotheses, recommended exams and lab tests versus physician records
evidence.effect: ChatGPT correct in 43% of diagnostic hypotheses, 5% of recommended supplementary exams, and 10% of laboratory tests; responses often partially accurate and unnecessarily detailed.
evidence.quote: When compared to physicians' records, ChatGPT provided correct responses in 43% of diagnostic hypotheses, 5% of recommended supplementary exams, and 10% of laboratory tests.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models for pharmacotherapy simulations: a mixed-methods study
evidence.outcome: Guideline alignment and pharmacotherapeutic accuracy of LLM-generated simulations judged by expert panels
evidence.effect: Clinical accuracy and safety was the limiting domain (58.3%) versus clinical reasoning (81.6%) and instructional design (82.5%). Guideline misalignment and pharmacotherapeutic inaccuracies found; 53 of 103 sessions passed all domains.
evidence.quote: Clinical accuracy and safety emerged as the limiting domain (58.3%) compared to clinical reasoning (81.6%) and instructional design (82.5%).

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's adherence to evidence-based heart failure guidelines: a comparative analysis using the 2023 ESC and 2022 ACC/AHA/HFSA recommendations
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-5 heart failure management responses with ESC and ACC/AHA/HFSA guidelines
evidence.effect: Of 38 responses, 20 (53%) fully concordant, 4 (11%) partially concordant, 8 (21%) discordant, 6 (16%) unsafe/harmful; errors included omission of GDMT and incomplete device therapy recommendations.
evidence.quote: Of the 38 responses, 20 (53%) were fully concordant, 4 (11%) partially concordant, 8 (21%) discordant, and 6 (16%) unsafe/harmful.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Turkish Emergency CT Impression Drafting: Quality, Critical Omissions, and Readability
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Omission of predefined critical findings in LLM-generated CT impressions by region and model
evidence.effect: Critical omissions were uncommon overall but showed model- and region-specific patterns; highest omission rate in abdominal CT for one model. No numeric rates in abstract.
evidence.quote: Critical omissions were uncommon overall but showed model- and region-specific patterns; the highest omission rate occurred in abdominal CT for one model.

evidence.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Chatbots Plan Therapeutic Ketogenic Diets for Children With Epilepsy?
evidence.venue: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of food choices and safety of AI-generated ketogenic diet plans
evidence.effect: For the MAD, chatbots exceeded net carbohydrate limits and provided inappropriate food suggestions; plans judged unsafe and unreliable by dietitians.
evidence.quote: For the MAD, the chatbots exceeded the specified net carbohydrate limits and provided inappropriate food suggestions.

evidence.title: Can a Large Language Model Grounded in Text-Based Agency-Specific Prehospital Protocols Provide Accurate Care Recommendations?
evidence.outcome: Omission of key clinical actions such as secondary treatable causes in pediatric cardiac arrest
evidence.effect: Five of nine major misses occurred in the pediatric OHCA case, mostly failure to prompt evaluation of secondary treatable causes.
evidence.quote: Five of nine major misses occurred during the pediatric OHCA case; the majority of these resulted from failure to prompt evaluation of secondary treatable causes.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenario prompts (169 expected patient care actions)

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models and retrieval-augmented generation for clinical reasoning in pediatric myopia: a 50-case real-world study
evidence.outcome: Baseline LLM alignment with clinical consensus and missing clinically significant content
evidence.effect: Baseline models opposed consensus up to 20% (Grok Base); missing content of great clinical significance 14-22% for baselines vs 2-4% for RAG.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, RAG significantly reduced the incidence of Missing Content of great clinical significance, with all RAG models scoring 2–4% in this category, compared to 14–22% for baseline models.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Model Performance in Appropriate Diagnostic Imaging Modality Selection
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: LLM imaging modality appropriateness versus ACR guideline criteria
evidence.effect: Appropriateness scores ranged 1.60-1.88 out of 2.00 with no significant pairwise differences; all LLMs selected appropriate modalities with reasonable justification.
evidence.quote: Appropriateness scores (range 1.60-1.88 out of 2.00) revealed no significant pairwise differences.

evidence.title: Accuracy of large language models in head and neck cancers: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT and Gemini in TNM staging and clinical decision support
evidence.outcome: LLM TNM staging and treatment plan accuracy versus AJCC 8th edition and tumor board decisions
evidence.effect: TNM staging accuracy ChatGPT 75.6%, Gemini 75.0%; treatment planning accuracy Gemini 78.9% vs ChatGPT 71.7% (p=0.043); staging error rate of 25% remains.
evidence.quote: However, a staging error rate of 25% remains a critical concern, potentially leading to inappropriate clinical pathways.

evidence.title: Persona Routing Associated With Fewer Safety and Monotonicity Violations in Simulated Emergency Large Language Model (LLM) Reasoning
evidence.outcome: contraindication and sequence safety violations
evidence.effect: LEAN baseline produced safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; 95% Wilson CI: 7.4%-25.7%; mean severity 0.39).
evidence.quote: In the router simulation, the lean baseline BASE_HL suggested the fewest tests (mean: 1.95) but produced contraindication/sequence safety violations in 8/56 scenarios (14.3%; 95% Wilson CI: 7.4%-25.7%; mean severity 0.39) (Table 3 ).
evidence.sample_unit: scenario-level runs (28 synthetic emergency vignettes x 2 replicates); 16 Base/Worse counterfactual comparisons per strategy

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of information quality, readability, and guideline consistency of large language model-generated educational content on hemodialysis complications: a cross-sectional assessment of generative AI-driven chatbots
evidence.outcome: Guideline concordance and omissions of guideline-recommended elements in LLM outputs
evidence.effect: Non-retrieval models often omitted guideline-recommended elements or gave less specific responses versus KDIGO-based reference statements; RAG models aligned relatively better.
evidence.quote: RAG-based models also showed relatively better alignment with reference guideline statements, whereas non-retrieval-based models more often omitted guideline-recommended elements or provided less specific responses.

evidence.title: Feasibility and challenges of large language model (LLM)-generated neonatal resuscitation simulations: a multicenter exploratory study
evidence.venue: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine

evidence.quote: DeepSeek manifested violations in NRP® algorithm.

evidence.title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
evidence.outcome: Major factual errors or critical omissions

evidence.quote: Safety audit error rates were low and did not differ significantly between models (1.25% vs. 3.75%, p = 0.25).

evidence.title: Benchmarking the readability, quality, and educational suitability of large language models in communicating pertussis

evidence.outcome: LLM severity grading errors, missing serious/lethal anomalies

evidence.title: Large language models approach clinician performance in ESC cardiovascular risk stratification: a vignette-based benchmark study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of guideline-based risk classification and direction of errors

evidence.title: Evaluating the Performance of Large Language Models for Breast Cancer Patient Education: A Comparative Study
evidence.venue: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and safety of LLM breast cancer answers
evidence.effect: No significant accuracy difference among models; ChatGPT-5.4-thinking scored significantly lower in safety; unsafe recommendations remain in answers.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-5.4-thinking scored significantly lower in safety, and Doubao-2.2-thinking had significantly lower reading difficulty, required age, and Chinese character count (adjusted P < 0.05).

evidence.title: ChatGPT response consistency to the 2025 ESC/EACTS guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease: A test-retest study using binary and multiple-choice questions

evidence.effect: Binary accuracy was 96.7% at both time points. Multiple-choice accuracy rose from 75.0% to 87.5%. Overall accuracy rose from 88.0% to 93.0%.
evidence.quote: However, the relatively high initial error rate in multiple-choice questions represents a limitation for clinical reliability.

evidence.title: Performance Evaluation of GPT-5, Grok 4, and DeepSeek R1 in Interpreting Complete Blood Count Reports for Hematologic Diseases: Retrospective Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Reasoning errors and unwarranted diagnostic inferences in correlation analysis and preliminary diagnosis tasks
evidence.effect: All models exhibited reasoning errors and deficiencies in correlation analysis and preliminary diagnosis, inferring disease status from isolated results without clinical integration.
evidence.quote: All models exhibited reasoning errors and varying degrees of deficiencies in the correlation analysis and preliminary diagnosis tasks, characterized by unwarranted inferences of disease status from isolated results without clinical integration.

evidence.title: Pilot Study Comparing Emergency Physician and Artificial Intelligence-supported Interpretations of Electrocardiograms
evidence.venue: The western journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: Concordance of AI ECG interpretation and management with emergency physician reference
evidence.effect: Agreement in 18 of 20 cases (90%), kappa 0.80; failed on fusion beats (0/1) and torsades (0/1), omitting IV magnesium sulfate despite recognizing the condition.
evidence.quote: In the torsades case, ChatGPT did not recommend intravenous magnesium sulfate-the standard first-line treatment-despite recognizing the condition.

evidence.title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Clinical knowledge errors, omissions, and missing safety warnings in guideline-based LBP responses
evidence.effect: Deepseek-V2.5 low-scoring responses: lack of safety warnings 16% (8/51), factual errors/hallucinations 12% (6/51); GPT-o3 harmful recommendations 7% (1/14).
evidence.quote: The most prominent causes of errors included: lack of safety warnings (Category 14: 16%, 8/51), factual errors/hallucinations (Category 1: 12%, 6/51), and incomplete or excessive content (Category 6: 10%, 5/51).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

evidence.title: Pre-implementation safety evaluation of an AI decision-support system for surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis
evidence.outcome: Guideline concordance and clinically significant prescribing risk of LLM surgical prophylaxis recommendations
evidence.effect: Clinically significant risk in 10% (2/20) of scenarios, including omitted anaerobic coverage and failure to redose in prolonged procedures; overall concordance 4/5, perfect dose accuracy, timing 70%.
evidence.quote: Clinically significant antimicrobial prescribing risk was identified in 10% of simulated scenarios (2/20), recognising wide confidence intervals due to the small sample size.

evidence.title: Large-Scale Evaluation of Five Large Language Models in Anesthesia Decision-Making for Hip Fracture Surgery
evidence.outcome: Consistency of LLM justifications and recommendations with current clinical evidence for anesthesia choice
evidence.effect: Free-text justifications frequently cited neuraxial benefits unsupported by recent randomized trials; most models issued strong neuraxial recommendations without clinical justification.
evidence.quote: However, free-text justifications frequently cited neuraxial benefits unsupported by recent randomized trials, and most models issued strong neuraxial recommendations despite a lack of clinical justification.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses to standardized hip fracture surgery vignettes

evidence.title: Evaluating the Quality of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Information on Cleft Lip and Palate: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy/completeness of LLM cleft lip and palate answers; outdated or incomplete clinical knowledge
evidence.effect: Median GQS 4.33 (GPT-4o) vs 5.00 (Gemini) in consensus domains, not significantly different (p=0.691); common errors included overgeneralized outcomes, outdated surgical timing, omitted multidisciplinary team roles.
evidence.quote: The most common inaccuracies were overgeneralization of outcomes, outdated surgical timing, and omission of multidisciplinary team roles.

evidence.title: An exploratory study of large language models in preoperative anesthesia assessment and planning for cardiac patients undergoing noncardiac surgery
evidence.outcome: LLM preoperative risk classification accuracy versus expert consensus (ASA, NYHA, RCRI, pulmonary risk)

evidence.quote: This exploratory study reveals that current LLMs exhibit suboptimal concordance with expert consensus in preoperative planning for complex cardiac cases.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Infectious Disease Decision-Making: From Examination to Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Completeness and prioritization of serious conditions in LLM differential diagnoses
evidence.effect: In Case 1, top three differentials from DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 did not include invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, a serious condition.
evidence.quote: In Case 1 ( Supplementary Table 1 in Supplementary material 2 ), which involved a patient with post-influenza pneumonia and a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the top three differential diagnoses generated by DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 did not include invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

evidence.title: Preliminary evaluation of DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-5.3 in selected PET/CT clinical scenarios: patient preparation, report interpretation, and diagnostic reasoning
evidence.outcome: Primary and differential diagnosis accuracy on difficult PET/CT cases
evidence.effect: Both models reached 10% primary diagnosis accuracy and 60% differential diagnosis accuracy on 10 difficult cases.
evidence.quote: For the 10 identical difficult cases, both models reached 10% primary diagnosis accuracy and 60% differential diagnosis accuracy.

evidence.title: Accuracy of an artificial intelligence chatbot in identifying congenital glaucoma from other ocular etiologies
evidence.outcome: Accuracy/appropriateness of clinical content on congenital glaucoma signs and symptoms
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4.0 acceptable 22/33 vs ChatGPT-3.5 9/33 (P=0.001); major incorrect information 0/33 vs 6/33 (P=0.02).
evidence.quote: A higher proportion of prompt responses from ChatGPT-4.0 were graded to be acceptable/appropriate than from ChatGPT-3.5 (22/33 vs 9/33 [P = 0.001]) among text-based queries.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Accuracy of ChatGPT-4o in Addressing Complex Clinical Questions Based on NCCN Guidelines for Rectal Adenocarcinoma
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers against NCCN rectal cancer guidelines across clinical domains
evidence.effect: 127/135 (94.1%) Correct and 121 (89.6%) Accurate; 8 responses (5.9%) partially or wholly incorrect, concentrated in multi-step conditional treatment decision points.
evidence.quote: Of 135 questions, 127 (94.1%; 95% CI, 88.7-97.0%) were Correct and 121 (89.6%; 95% CI, 83.3-93.7%) were Accurate.

evidence.title: Assessing Readability and DISCERN Quality of Osteoporosis Education Materials Generated by ChatGPT and Deepseek for Diverse Health Literacy Levels: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Guideline concordance and completeness of LLM osteoporosis content versus NOF/IOF guidelines
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 13.24/18 (73.7%); no hallucinations detected; inaccuracies mostly omissions, lowest in pharmacotherapy (2.04/3) and screening (2.11/3).
evidence.quote: No output received a score of 0 in any domain, and no hallucinations (i.e., factually incorrect statements contrary to established guidelines) were detected in any output.

evidence.title: Gut Instincts, Machine Decisions: Evaluating AI Accuracy in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM diagnosis and treatment recommendations against Rome IV MDCP guidance
evidence.effect: Diagnostic accuracy 65% to 74%; treatment accuracy 41% to 54%; no significant differences between models.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy across models demonstrated Perplexity at 74%, ChatGPT and Google Gemini at 72% respectively, and Microsoft Copilot and OpenEvidence at 65% respectively.

evidence.title: Assessing the concordance between ChatGPT-4 and EAU guidelines indications in bladder cancer management: a real-world study
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-4 therapeutic recommendations with EAU guidelines-based urologist plans
evidence.effect: Overall agreement poor (Cohen's K=-0.06); first-time BCa K=0.23; MIBC K=0.88; recurrent K=-0.24; II look TURBT K=-0.6; aligned with guidelines for early radical cystectomy in only 3 of 21 cases.
evidence.quote: Overall agreement between urologist and ChatGPT recommendations was poor (Cohen's K=-0.06).

evidence.title: Potential and Pitfalls of Multimodal Large Language Models in Cerebral Palsy Hip Surveillance: A Radiographic Interpretation Study Assessing Educational Utility
evidence.outcome: Radiographic interpretation accuracy and management recommendation specificity of MLLMs for CP hip displacement
evidence.effect: Diagnostic hallucinations observed (Claude misidentified non-operative cases as bilateral hip replacements); recommendations were generic and failed to measure or apply migration percentage thresholds.
evidence.quote: While management recommendations were clinically relevant, they remained generic rather than patient-specific, failing to measure or apply migration percentage thresholds.
evidence.sample_unit: deidentified pediatric pelvic radiographs (with 9 caregiver prompts each; ~95 responses per model)

evidence.title: The illusion of competence: Evaluating the clinical reasoning of large language models in pediatric gastroenterology
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
evidence.outcome: Currency and accuracy of clinical knowledge in LLM outputs
evidence.effect: All three models achieved perfect diagnostic accuracy (median 2.00, IQR 2.00-2.00), but qualitative analysis found temporal obsolescence.
evidence.quote: Qualitative analysis revealed critical pharmacological dosing errors, contextual blindness, temporal obsolescence, and a high frequency of fabricated citations.

evidence.title: Patient and physician perspectives on large language model generated responses about brain aneurysm
evidence.venue: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated consistency with current medical knowledge and guidelines, and omission of key points, in LLM answers
evidence.effect: ChatGPT and Gemini differed in consistency with current medical knowledge and practice guidelines (p = 0.001), omittance of key points (p < 0.001), and clinically relevant detail (p < 0.001); physicians rated LLM responses similar or somewhat worse than their own.
evidence.quote: Importantly, differences were found in consistency with current medical knowledge and practice guidelines (p = 0.001), omittance of key points (p < 0.001), and amount of clinically relevant detail included (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: survey respondents (community members and physicians) rating LLM responses to brain aneurysm FAQs

evidence.title: Comparison of large language models in the management of pediatric ureteropelvic junction obstruction: a comparative analysis of 125 clinical scenarios
evidence.outcome: LLM clinical accuracy against international guidelines for pediatric UPJO management, by model
evidence.effect: ChatGPT clinical accuracy 4.13 +/- 1.31 and reliability 4.08 +/- 1.30, closest to guidelines; Copilot accuracy 3.49 +/- 1.67 with frequent clinical inaccuracies despite the highest readability.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated significantly higher scores in clinical accuracy (4.13 +/- 1.31) and reliability (4.08 +/- 1.30) compared to its counterparts, showing the closest alignment with international guidelines.

evidence.title: Quality of AI-generated exercise awareness messages for older adults aligned with the ICFSR consensus: a comparative study of three LLMs
evidence.venue: European review of aging and physical activity : official journal of the European Group for Research into Elderly and Physical Activity
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and safety of LLM exercise messages against ICFSR consensus
evidence.effect: Overall scores Claude 4.63, ChatGPT-4 4.55, Deepseek 4.15 on 5-point scale; Claude accuracy 4.58 ± 0.64; Deepseek lower and more variable.
evidence.quote: Claude achieved the overall scores from both evaluators at 4.63 ± 0.55 and 4.60 ± 0.55, followed by ChatGPT-4 at 4.55 ± 0.50 and 4.48 ± 0.53 and Deepseek at 4.15 ± 0.87 and 4.17 ± 0.86.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of Large Language Models for Orthopedic-Related Rare Diseases and Their Impact on Physicians' Diagnostic Accuracy: 2-Stage Comparative Evaluation Study Based on the Chinese Rare Disease Catalog
evidence.outcome: LLM primary-diagnosis accuracy on orthopedic rare diseases
evidence.effect: Claude Sonnet 4.5, ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro each 90% (36/40); DeepSeek-V3.2 67.5% (27/40); Cochran Q P<.001.
evidence.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.5, ChatGPT-5.0, Gemini 2.5 Pro each achieved 90% (36/40) primary-diagnosis accuracy, whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 achieved 67.5% (27/40; Cochran Q P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: orthopedic physicians (27 intermediate, 15 senior) diagnosing 40 rare disease cases

evidence.title: Comparative Assessment of Performance of Domain-Specific and Primed Versus Non-Primed Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Clinical Decision-Making in Injuries to the Primary Dentition: An Exploratory Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
evidence.outcome: agreement with IADT guideline recommendations
evidence.effect: All chatbots had complete diagnostic accuracy; Dental Trauma Evo had 100% immediate management accuracy, while general-purpose models had minor inaccuracies.
evidence.quote: The domain-specific chatbot achieved 100% accuracy in immediate management decisions, while minor inaccuracies were observed among general-purpose models.

evidence.quote: However, its recommendations of antiemetic agents as per the SAMBA guidelines are inconsistent, necessitating human oversight for guideline-based management.

evidence.title: Evaluation and comparison of large language model responses to patient questions after diagnosis of high-risk human papillomavirus infection: an expert-rated digital patient education study
evidence.outcome: Proportion of LLM responses without major error or potential harm on HPV questions
evidence.effect: 42/45 (93.3%) ChatGPT and 38/45 (84.4%) DeepSeek-V3 responses had no major error or potential harm; exploratory question-level risks in HPV16/18 positivity, normal cytology, partner management, pregnancy.
evidence.quote: Responses without major error or potential harm occurred in 42/45 (93.3%; 95% CI, 81.7-98.6%) ChatGPT responses and 38/45 (84.4%; 70.5-93.5%) DeepSeek-V3 responses (risk difference, 8.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -13.3 to 31.1; p = 0.344).

evidence.title: Guideline-concordant decision support in abdominal radiology: An expert-based evaluation of Gemini
evidence.outcome: Guideline concordance of impression and final category
evidence.effect: Overall impression concordance was 85.0 % (170/200), and final-category concordance was 77.5 % (155/200); concordance lower with greater case difficulty (both p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Overall impression concordance was 85.0 % (170/200), and final-category concordance was 77.5 % (155/200).

evidence.title: Safety in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Evaluating Large Language Model Adherence to Antithrombotic Medication and Regional Anesthesia Guidelines
evidence.outcome: LLM adherence to 2025 ASRA antithrombotic hold/resumption guidelines in vignettes
evidence.effect: Concordance 64% ChatGPT vs 62% Gemini; dangerous errors 20% ChatGPT and 12% Gemini; ChatGPT omitted time in 16%; Gemini conservative errors 22%.
evidence.quote: Both models produced potentially dangerous recommendations in 12-20% of scenarios.

evidence.title: Evaluation and comparison of large language model responses to common discharge questions from patients with acute coronary syndrome after percutaneous coronary intervention: An expert-rated comparative study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and guideline concordance of LLM post-PCI discharge answers
evidence.effect: ChatGPT scored higher than DeepSeek in accuracy, guideline concordance, completeness, total quality (adjusted P=0.015, 0.015, 0.019, 0.005). Five-domain satisfactory rates 100.0% vs 90.7% (P=0.125).
evidence.quote: After pairing and Holm adjustment, ChatGPT scored higher in accuracy, guideline concordance, completeness, and total quality (adjusted P=0.015, 0.015, 0.019, and 0.005).

evidence.title: Multidisciplinary dental treatment planning by artificial intelligence: A comparative evaluation

evidence.quote: DeepSeek achieved the highest principal diagnosis matching rate (66/85, 77.6%), followed by Gemini (59/85, 69.4%) and ChatGPT (52/85, 61.2%).

evidence.outcome: Alignment of LLM answers with Chinese bladder cancer guidelines; harmful or contradictory advice

evidence.quote: No model produced harmful advice or directly contradicted guideline recommendations.

evidence.effect: Experts made 1 critical error; LLMs made 5-9 each (Q = 17.10, P = 0.004). Experts made no critical errors in high-risk scenarios; all LLMs made at least one.

evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-5 antibiotic prophylaxis answers with AHA/AAE/ADA guidelines, rated by one endodontist
evidence.effect: Full agreement in 10/17 (58.8%), partial in 4 (23.5%) due to unnecessary expansion of indications, disagreement in 3 (17.6%), mainly immunocompromised cases; no response deemed clinically unsafe.

evidence.title: Laboratory Medicine Decision Support-Beyond Exam Passing: A Blinded 100-Case Text-Based Benchmark of Diagnostic Accuracy, Management Quality, and Safety for ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek-LLM Decision Support in Laboratory Medicine
evidence.outcome: Unsafe or guideline-discordant recommendations and primary diagnostic concordance in laboratory medicine vignettes
evidence.effect: Unsafe or guideline-discordant recommendations in 2% (ChatGPT-5.2), 4% (Gemini), 5% (DeepSeek); fully concordant primary diagnoses in 88%, 84%, 82% of cases.

evidence.effect: At least one platform missed the reference diagnosis in 9/15 vignettes; all three missed porphyria. 82.2% of CUS ratings were in categories 4-5.
evidence.quote: In the single-query diagnostic assessment, at least one platform missed the reference diagnosis in 9/15 vignettes, and all three missed porphyria.

evidence.title: Facts Fade Fast: Evaluating Memorization of Outdated Medical Knowledge in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: LLM reliance on outdated medical knowledge on questions where consensus changed

evidence.title: Large language models management of medications: three performance analyses
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of identifying drug-drug interaction pairs for a given medication regimen

evidence.title: Simulating Viva Voce Examinations to Evaluate Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Failure modes in LLM diagnostic reasoning, including failing to screen for critical conditions
evidence.effect: Identified failure modes: fixation on initial hypotheses, inappropriate investigation ordering, premature diagnostic closure, and failing to screen for critical conditions.
evidence.quote: Our analysis identified several failure modes that mirror common cognitive errors in clinical practice, including: (1) fixation on initial hypotheses, (2) inappropriate investigation ordering, (3) premature diagnostic closure, and (4) failing to screen for critical conditions.

evidence.title: RxSafeBench: Identifying Medication Safety Issues of Large Language Models in Simulated Consultation
evidence.outcome: LLM ability to choose safe medications given contraindications and drug interactions in simulated consultations
evidence.effect: Current LLMs struggle to integrate contraindication and interaction knowledge, especially when risks are implied rather than explicit; no numeric results in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Results show that current LLMs struggle to integrate contraindication and interaction knowledge, especially when risks are implied rather than explicit.

evidence.title: A Decade-Scale Benchmark Evaluating LLMs' Clinical Practice Guidelines Detection and Adherence in Multi-turn Conversations
evidence.outcome: LLM adherence to clinical practice guideline recommendations in multi-turn conversations

evidence.quote: The adherence rates range from 21.8% to 63.2% in different models, indicating a large gap between knowing the guidelines and being able to apply them.

evidence.title: WHBench: Evaluating Frontier LLMs with Expert-in-the-Loop Validation on Women's Health Topics
evidence.outcome: LLM clinical accuracy and guideline adherence on women's health scenarios, including outdated guidelines and unsafe omissions
evidence.effect: No model mean performance exceeded 75 percent; best model reached 72.1 percent. Top models showed low fully correct rates and substantial variation in harm rates.
evidence.quote: Across 3,102 attempted responses (3,100 scored), no model mean performance exceeds 75 percent; the best model reaches 72.1 percent.

evidence.title: Teaching LLMs Brazilian Healthcare: Injecting Knowledge from Official Clinical Guidelines

evidence.effect: Current LLMs perform poorly on guideline-specific knowledge; the adapted 14B model reached 83.9% on HealthBench-BR and 85.4% on PCDT-QA, outperforming GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Google AI Overview.
evidence.quote: Yet current LLMs perform poorly on this guideline-specific knowledge, and no benchmark evaluates clinical recall grounded in Brazilian Portuguese protocols.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Lack Temporal Awareness of Medical Knowledge
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on time-specific guideline knowledge, current versus historical recommendations
evidence.effect: Accuracy on up-to-date knowledge declines linearly over time. Historical knowledge accuracy is only 25.37%-53.89% of up-to-date knowledge. Predictions fluctuate across neighboring years.
evidence.quote: LLMs consistently struggle more with recalling outdated historical medical knowledge than with up-to-date recommendations: accuracy of historical knowledge is only 25.37%-53.89% of up-to-date knowledge

evidence.title: GlobalDentBench: A Multinational Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Clinical Reasoning in Dentistry with Expert Calibration
evidence.outcome: Safety of LLM-generated clinical recommendations in real-world dental cases
evidence.effect: Overall unsafe rate of 31.01% in LLM-generated clinical recommendations, with 4.51% posing risks of irreversible patient harm, particularly in orthodontics.
evidence.quote: More critically, risk analysis of real-world dental cases demonstrated an alarming overall unsafe rate of 31.01% in LLM-generated clinical recommendations, with 4.51% posing risks of irreversible patient harm and risks particularly pronounced in specialties such as orthodontics.

evidence.title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
evidence.outcome: Rate of recommending banned or withdrawn drugs in default LLM configurations
evidence.effect: All models showed high hallucination rates in default configurations, consistently selecting banned drugs that matched training data patterns (no numeric default rate given in abstract).
evidence.quote: In default configurations, all models showed high hallucination rates, consistently selecting banned drugs that matched training data patterns.

evidence.title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
evidence.outcome: LLM outputs failing guideline constraints and evidence-path checks in type 2 diabetes vignettes
evidence.effect: Baseline outputs failed benchmark-defined evidence-path checks in 35% of cases for GPT-4o-mini and 33% for GPT-4o.
evidence.quote: Across 100 structured vignettes spanning diagnosis, medication safety, and adversarial lifestyle conflicts, baseline outputs failed benchmark-defined evidence-path checks in 35% of cases for GPT-4o-mini and 33% for GPT-4o.

evidence.title: Probing the Surgical Competence of LLMs: A global health study leveraging AfriMedQA benchmarks
evidence.outcome: Omission of local clinical guidelines and procedural reasoning failures in LLM answers
evidence.effect: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures and omission of local clinical guidelines.
evidence.quote: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures, omission of local clinical guidelines, and overconfident but incorrect answers.
evidence.country: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and other African countries (AfriMed-QA benchmark; authored by African medical professors)

evidence.title: Benchmarking eye health advice from generative artificial intelligence in terms of factual accuracy, safety, comprehensiveness and readability
evidence.outcome: Factual alignment, omissions, and guideline consistency of genAI eye advice versus leaflets
evidence.effect: Higher factual alignment (GPT-5 37.4%, Gemini 3 36.2%, leaflets 30.7%) and fewer omissions (6.7, 7.0 vs 7.9), but guideline inconsistencies and underreported complications.
evidence.quote: Both genAI models showed higher factual alignment than clinical leaflets (GPT-5 = 37.4%, Gemini 3 = 36.2%, leaflets = 30.7%; both p < 0.001) and fewer omissions (GPT-5 = 6.7, Gemini 3 = 7.0, leaflets = 7.9; both p < 0.001).

evidence.title: not-yet-known not-yet-known not-yet-known unknown Evaluating the accuracy of large language models on ESGO/ESTRO/ESP guidelines for cervical cancer: are large language models reliable assistants in clinical practice?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers versus ESGO/ESTRO/ESP cervical cancer guidelines (GQS 1-5)
evidence.effect: GQS 5 rates: ChatGPT-4.0 42%, Gemini-2.0 30%, DeepSeek-R1 28%. Mean GQS 3.02 for DeepSeek-R1 vs 3.74 for ChatGPT-4.0 (p=0.022).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.0 achieved the highest performance, with 42% of responses rated GQS 5, followed by Gemini-2.0 (30%) and DeepSeek-R1 (28%).

evidence.title: Frontier Large Language Models for Comprehensive Medication Review in CKD Patients with Polypharmacy: A Trap-Embedded Synthetic Benchmark
evidence.outcome: Detection of clinically important drug-related problems and omissions in medication review
evidence.effect: Safety-critical omission rate 22% to 48%; phosphate binder timing detected 11% and hyperkalemia combinations 33%.
evidence.quote: Phosphate binder timing (11%) and hyperkalemia combinations (33%) were poorly detected across all models.

evidence.title: Comparing AI-generated and evidence-based recommendations for chronic pain and tDCS parameters: a descriptive qualitative study
evidence.outcome: Concordance of AI pharmacological recommendations with guideline and systematic-review evidence for chronic pain
evidence.effect: Full concordance in 38.5% of cases, partial concordance in 53.8%, no concordance in 7.7%; tDCS parameter recommendations varied, especially electrode montage and session standardization.
evidence.quote: Regarding pharmacological management, full concordance between AI-generated recommendations and evidence-based standards was observed in 38.5% of cases, partial concordance in 53.8%, and no concordance in 7.7%.

evidence.title: A collective capability boundary in frontier large language models on guideline-conformant and case-specific oncology decision-making
evidence.outcome: Share of oncology guideline and case items answered correctly by none of nine LLMs
evidence.effect: 42.1% (Wilson 95% CI 40.0%–44.3%) of all items were answered correctly by none; 35.7% of 1,586 NCCN guideline items and 66.4% of 419 colorectal cancer case items.
evidence.quote: Treating the nine as a pooled super-model, 42.1% (Wilson 95% CI40.0%–44.3%) of all items—35.7% of the 1,586 NCCN guideline items and 66.4%of the 419 colorectal cancer case items—were answered correctly by none;
evidence.sample_unit: oncology decision points (1,586 NCCN guideline items and 419 colorectal cancer case items)

evidence.title: Clinical Reliability and Consistency of Large Language Models in Prosthodontics: An Expert Evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini
evidence.outcome: Factual accuracy of LLM responses to prosthodontics questions rated by three examiners
evidence.effect: Models showed difficulties with specialized terminology and complex concepts, with occasional hallucinations and erroneous or incomplete responses. Mean accuracy difference between models not significant (p = 0.109).
evidence.quote: Both models showed difficulties with specialized terminology and complex concepts, with the occasional presence of hallucinations and erroneous or incomplete responses.

evidence.title: MedPI: Evaluating AI Systems in Medical Patient-facing Interactions
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on differential diagnosis and other dimensions in simulated patient-clinician conversations
evidence.effect: All 9 LLMs showed low performance across a variety of dimensions, particularly differential diagnosis, across 7,097 simulated conversations scored on 105 dimensions (1-4 scale).
evidence.quote: For all LLMs, we observe low performance across a variety of dimensions, in particular on differential diagnosis.

evidence.title: When AI Meets the FDA: An Evaluation of Large Language Models Performance in Regulatory and Clinical Trial Data Extraction, Synthesis, and Analysis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate of LLM extraction of FDA regulatory and trial information
evidence.effect: Accuracy 66.7% Gemini 2.5 Pro, 51.9% ChatGPT-4o, 37.0% DeepSeek R1 (p<0.001); hallucination was the most frequent error type across models.
evidence.quote: Hallucination was the most frequent error type across models.

evidence.title: RheumBench: A Specialist-Validated Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Rheumatology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic top-1 and top-3 accuracy on rheumatology cases; severity of errors
evidence.effect: Top-1 accuracy peaked at 57.1% (GPT-5.6 Sol) and top-3 at 67.1% (Claude Fable 5). Potentially severe errors, mostly omissions, occurred with all systems.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic top-1 accuracy reached 57.1% (GPT-5.6 Sol), while top-3 accuracy reached 67.1% (Claude Fable 5).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical cases (70 diagnostic, 30 management; 1,020 rubric criteria)

evidence.title: Evaluating GPT-4o Model Proficiency and Clinical Reasoning for Antimicrobial Stewardship in Dentistry
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o accuracy on dental antibiotic prescribing questions and justification content completeness and harm
evidence.effect: GPT-4o answered 72% correctly; experts rated 95.4% of justifications positively; missing content was the main weakness (7.8%); 7.1% of justifications showed moderate-to-severe potential for harm.
evidence.quote: Missing content was the main weakness (7.8%), and 7.1% of justifications showed a moderate-to-severe potential for harm.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4 in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Board Examination using the CVSA Model
evidence.outcome: Correctness and completeness of clinical knowledge in open-ended OHNS board questions
evidence.effect: Passing mark averaging 75% across three trials, but responses were often only partially correct, with hallucinations and self-conflicting answers observed.
evidence.quote: While demonstrating considerable consistency in regenerating answers, it often provided only partially correct responses.

evidence.title: Performance of Multimodal GPT-4V on USMLE with Image: Potential for Imaging Diagnostic Support with Explanations
evidence.outcome: Explanation errors when GPT-4V answered incorrectly (made-up text, inferencing errors, image misunderstanding)
evidence.effect: Among wrong answers, 18.2% had made-up text; 45.5% had inferencing errors; 76.3% had image misunderstandings.
evidence.quote: However, when GPT-4V answered incorrectly, the quality of generated explanation was poor: 18.2% wrong answers had made-up text; 45.5% had inferencing errors; and 76.3% had image misunderstandings.

evidence.title: Evaluating GPT as an Adjunct for Radiologic Decision Making: GPT-4 Versus GPT-3.5 in a Breast Imaging Pilot
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM imaging recommendations with ACR Appropriateness Criteria guidelines
evidence.effect: Breast screening OE score 1.830/2 for both models; SATA 88.9% (GPT-3.5) vs 98.4% (GPT-4). Breast pain OE 1.125 vs 1.666/2; SATA 58.3% vs 77.7%.
evidence.quote: For breast pain, ChatGPT-3.5 achieved an average OE score of 1.125 (out of 2) and a SATA average percentage correct of 58.3%, as compared with an average OE score of 1.666 (out of 2) and a SATA average percentage correct of 77.7%.
evidence.sample_unit: prompts (ACR Appropriateness Criteria clinical variants, three replicates each)

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Performance of Generative AI Large Language Models ChatGPT, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing Chat in Supporting Evidence-Based Dentistry: Comparative Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, completeness, and currency of LLM dental clinical knowledge versus guidelines
evidence.effect: LLMs delivered irrelevant, vague, outdated, or not fully accurate information against guideline-based rubric; ChatGPT-4 scored best.
evidence.quote: The evaluators noted instances where the LLMs delivered irrelevant information, vague answers, or information that was not fully accurate.

evidence.title: Use of ChatGPT for Determining Clinical and Surgical Treatment of Lumbar Disc Herniation With Radiculopathy: A North American Spine Society Guideline Comparison
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT responses with NASS guideline recommendations for lumbar disc herniation
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 accurate in 15/29 (52%); ChatGPT-4 accurate in 17/29 (59%); incompleteness in 11 (38%) and 8 (23%) responses.
evidence.quote: Out of 29 clinical guidelines evaluated, ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated accuracy in 15 responses (52%), while ChatGPT-4 achieved accuracy in 17 responses (59%).

evidence.title: Generative artificial intelligence and non-pharmacological bias: an experimental study on cancer patient sexual health communications
evidence.outcome: Concordance of chatbot recommendations with clinical guidelines on pharmacological versus non-pharmacological interventions
evidence.effect: Both bots favored counselling over pharmacological options despite guidelines recommending both; OR=47.3 in Bot1 (95% CI 9.55 to 233.81) and 97.2 in Bot2 (95% CI 11.72 to 806.04), p<0.001.
evidence.quote: For sexual response and sexual function, the guidelines recommended both pharmacological and non-pharmacological intervention for them, non-pharmacological intervention (counselling) was significantly more frequently than pharmacological intervention (OR=47.3 in Bot1 (95% CI 9.55 to 233.81, p<0.001), 97.2 in Bot2 (95% CI 11.72 to 806.04, p<0.001)).

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's efficacy in assessing the safety of non-prescription medications and supplements in patients with kidney disease
evidence.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT drug safety classification with Micromedex for kidney disease patients
evidence.effect: Agreement with Micromedex was 64.5% for ChatGPT-3.5 and 81.4% for ChatGPT-4. ChatGPT-3.5 flagged 11 (8.9%) as potentially harmful versus Micromedex 35 (28.2%).
evidence.quote: The overall agreement between Micromedex and ChatGPT-3.5 was 64.5% and ChatGPT-4 demonstrated a higher agreement at 81.4%.

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT as a Tool for Answering Clinical Questions in Pharmacy Practice
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT clinical knowledge accuracy on pharmacy patient case and drug information questions
evidence.effect: Overall score 21/44 (47.73%); patient case category scored 20%, enhanced prompt drug information 33%, while calculations 100%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT scored higher in pharmacy calculation (100%), drug information (83%), and top 200 drugs (80%) categories and lower in drug information enhanced prompt (33%) and patient case (20%) categories.

evidence.title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
evidence.outcome: General LLM accuracy against current clinical guidelines for osteoarthritis management
evidence.effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 accuracy was 0.01 and 0.07 on treatment strategy QA and 0.03 and 0.01 on real-case QA; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were unsatisfactory on guideline-based questions.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of GPT-3.5 in GIQA, MOQA, TSQA, and RCQA was 0.26, 0.22, 0.01, and 0.03, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT-3.5's Knowledge in Oncology: Comparative Study with ASCO-SEP Benchmarks
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-3.5 accuracy on oncology multiple-choice questions from ASCO-SEP
evidence.effect: 56.1% (583/1040) correct overall; lowest in gastrointestinal cancer (102/209; 48.8%); highest in developmental therapeutics (8/10; 80%); no significant difference across diagnosis, treatment, other (P=.16)
evidence.quote: Overall, ChatGPT-3.5 achieved a score of 56.1% (583/1040) for the correct answers provided.

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models on Medical Oncology Examination Questions
evidence.outcome: Errors in LLM oncology answers, including outdated knowledge from recent publications, and potential clinical harm
evidence.effect: Incorrect responses most commonly involved information retrieval errors, particularly with recent publications; 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%) would have medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm.
evidence.quote: Incorrect responses were most commonly associated with errors in information retrieval, particularly with recent publications, followed by erroneous reasoning and reading comprehension.

evidence.title: AI-Generated Content in Cancer Symptom Management: A Comparative Analysis Between ChatGPT and NCCN
evidence.venue: Journal of pain and symptom management
evidence.outcome: Agreement between ChatGPT symptom management recommendations and NCCN guidelines
evidence.effect: Mean percent agreement between NCCN and ChatGPT was 37.3% (range 16.7%-81.8%); NCCN gave more specific medication recommendations; ChatGPT recommended medications for constipation and diarrhea not recommended by NCCN.
evidence.quote: The mean percent agreement between NCCN and ChatGPT recommendations was 37.3% (range 16.7%-81.8%).
evidence.sample_unit: cancer symptoms (NCCN guideline sections compared with ChatGPT responses)

evidence.title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making
evidence.outcome: LLM adherence to diagnostic and treatment guidelines
evidence.effect: LLMs followed neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines.
evidence.quote: We show that current state-of-the-art LLMs do not accurately diagnose patients across all pathologies (performing significantly worse than physicians), follow neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and cannot interpret laboratory results, thus posing a serious risk to the health of patients.

evidence.title: Do ChatGPT and Gemini Provide Appropriate Recommendations for Pediatric Orthopaedic Conditions?
evidence.outcome: Agreement of LLM responses with AAOS pediatric orthopaedic clinical practice guidelines
evidence.effect: ChatGPT and Gemini agreed with AAOS CPGs at 67% and 69%; no significant difference between models; neutral statements or disagreement rate was substantial.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT and Gemini performed similarly, agreeing with the AAOS CPGs at a rate of 67% and 69%.

evidence.title: Currently Available Large Language Models Do Not Provide Musculoskeletal Treatment Recommendations That Are Concordant With Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence.venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM treatment recommendations with AAOS clinical practice guidelines
evidence.effect: 135 responses (70.3%) concordant, 43 (22.4%) indeterminate, 14 (7.3%) discordant; ChatGPT-4 79.2% concordant, Mistral-7B 58.3%; no significant difference across LLMs (P = .12).
evidence.quote: Overall, 135 responses (70.3%) were concordant, 43 (22.4%) were indeterminate, and 14 (7.3%) were discordant.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (48 AAOS guideline recommendations x 4 LLMs)

evidence.title: Discrepancies in ChatGPT's Hip Fracture Recommendations in Older Adults for 2021 AAOS Evidence-Based Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT recommendation strengths versus 2021 AAOS guidelines
evidence.effect: Accuracy 0.684, 0.579, 0.632 for outputs A, B, C; precision 0.740, 0.737, 0.718.
evidence.quote: Regarding the strengths of the recommendation compared with the 2021 AAOS guidelines, we observed accuracy of 0.684, 0.579, and 0.632 for outputs A, B, and C, respectively.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Diagnosing and Managing Vascular Surgery Patients: An Experimental Study Using the GPT-4 Model
evidence.outcome: Outdated or incorrect clinical knowledge in GPT-4 answers to vascular surgery scenarios
evidence.effect: GPT-4 quoted incorrect or outdated information in 14% of failed cases and could not comprehend context, nuances, and medical classification systems in 11%; over 65% of 385 questions answered correctly.
evidence.quote: The AI model also quoted incorrect or outdated information in 14% of cases and showed an inability to comprehend context, nuances, and medical classification systems in 11% of the cases.

evidence.title: Risk stratification of potential drug interactions involving common over-the-counter medications and herbal supplements by a large language model
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and agreement of LLM drug interaction risk ratings versus Lexicomp reference
evidence.effect: All models underperformed, with accuracies below 50% and poor Cohen's kappa agreement with Lexicomp; GPT-4 and GPT-4o modestly better than GPT-3.5 at identifying higher-risk interactions.
evidence.quote: Our findings reveal that all models generally underperform, with accuracies below 50% and poor agreement with Lexicomp standards as measured by Cohen's kappa.
evidence.sample_unit: drug interaction pairs (43 Rx-OTC, 30 Rx-herbal supplement)

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5 and Google Gemini on PCOS assessment and management based on recommendations from the 2023 guideline
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and quality of chatbot answers versus 2023 PCOS guideline recommendations
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 and ChatGPT-3.5 scored higher than Gemini in accuracy and quality (p = 0.001, p < 0.001 and p = 0.007, p < 0.001 respectively).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 and ChatGPT-3.5 attained higher scores in accuracy and quality compared to Gemini (p = 0.001, p < 0.001 and p = 0.007, p < 0.001 respectively).

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Generative Pre-Trained Transformer Models in Oncogene-Driven Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Introducing the Generative Artificial Intelligence Performance Score
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT NSCLC treatment recommendations versus NCCN guidelines, including hallucination rate
evidence.effect: GPT-4 base score 90% vs 60% for GPT-3.5; hallucinations 34% vs 53%; G-PS 0.34 vs -0.15 (P<.01).
evidence.quote: Analyzing 160 responses, generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4 outperformed GPT-3.5, showing higher base score (90% v 60%; P < .01) and fewer hallucinations (34% v 53%; P < .01).

evidence.title: The Ability of Large Language Models to Generate Patient Information Materials for Retinopathy of Prematurity: Evaluation of Readability, Accuracy, and Comprehensiveness
evidence.outcome: Consistency of LLM clinical content with local (Turkish) screening guidelines
evidence.effect: GPT-4.0 gave screening criteria (<30 weeks or <1,500 g) matching UK, not TOA criteria (<34 weeks or <1,700 g), risking misinformation.
evidence.quote: GPT-4.0’s response for this question (“infants born before 30 weeks or weighing less than 1,500 grams”) was comparable to the screening criteria employed in the United Kingdom but not with the TOA standards for Türkiye.

evidence.title: Comparing ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4's alignments with the German evidence-based S3 guideline for adult soft tissue sarcoma
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and adequacy of LLM answers against guideline-derived sarcoma questions, scored by experts
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 outperformed ChatGPT-3.5 in accuracy (median 5.5 vs 5.0) and adequacy (5.0 vs 4.0); both occasionally gave misleading, potentially life-threatening information.
evidence.quote: Despite their potential as a supportive tool, both models occasionally offered misleading and potentially life-threatening information.

evidence.title: Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus and Diaphyseal Femur Fractures: A Comparative Analysis of Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer and Google Gemini Recommendations Versus American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Chatbot accuracy and completeness versus AAOS clinical practice guideline recommendations
evidence.effect: Accurate in 11/13 (ChatGPT-4.0), 9/13 (ChatGPT-3.5), 11/13 (Gemini); incomplete in 3/13, 4/13, 4/13; no significant differences (accuracy P=0.533).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.0, ChatGPT-3.5, and Google Gemini were accurate in 11/13, 9/13, and 11/13, supplementary in 13/13, 11/13, and 13/13, and incomplete in 3/13, 4/13, and 4/13 recommendations, respectively.

evidence.title: From RAGs to riches: Utilizing large language models to write documents for clinical trials
evidence.outcome: Adherence of off-the-shelf LLM recommendations to current regulatory guidance
evidence.effect: Off-the-shelf LLM scored just over 40% on clinical thinking and logic; example excluded HIV, diabetes, liver and kidney disease patients from a TB trial contrary to FDA guidance.
evidence.quote: However, for clinical thinking and logic , the off-the-shelf LLM scores poorly (assessment score just over 40%), meaning that recommendations from the off-the-shelf LLM often do not follow the latest regulatory guidance or contain other errors.

evidence.title: Using Large Language Models in the Diagnosis of Acute Cholecystitis: Assessing Accuracy and Guidelines Compliance
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy against Tokyo Guidelines 2018 on acute cholecystitis questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT4.0 gave accurate and comprehensive answers for 4/10 (40%), accurate but not comprehensive for 5/10 (50%), and one (10%) partially accurate, partially inaccurate; no entirely inaccurate answers.
evidence.quote: One response (10%) was rated as "partially accurate, partially inaccurate."

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models' Concordance With Guidelines on Olfaction
evidence.outcome: LLM concordance and accuracy versus ICAR-O olfaction guideline recommendations
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy 1.85 (ChatGPT) and 1.48 (Gemini) out of 2; concordance 78.57% (33/42) ChatGPT and 66.67% (28/42) Gemini; ChatGPT more accurate than Gemini (p = 0.001).
evidence.quote: However, overall, both platforms did not consistently align with clinical guidelines.

evidence.title: Assessing AI in Various Elements of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS)-Guided Ankle Fracture Treatment: A Comparative Analysis with Expert Agreement
evidence.outcome: LLM answers' alignment with expert consensus guidelines on ERAS ankle fracture management
evidence.effect: ChatGPT aligned with expert consensus in 29/35 (82.9%); iFlytek Spark in 22/35 (62.9%). Discrepancies in intraoperative blood pressure management and preoperative antiemetic selection.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated higher alignment with expert consensus (29/35 questions, 82.9%), particularly in comprehensive perioperative recommendations, detailed medical rationales, and structured treatment plans.

evidence.title: Assessing bias in AI-driven psychiatric recommendations: A comparative cross-sectional study of chatbot-classified and CANMAT 2023 guideline for adjunctive therapy in difficult-to-treat depression
evidence.outcome: Agreement of chatbot adjunctive-therapy classifications with CANMAT 2023 guidelines (Cohen's kappa)
evidence.effect: Gemini 2.0 Flash kappa 0.82 (SE 0.052); OpenAI o1 kappa 0.746 (SE 0.057). Overestimated quetiapine and lithium; underestimated modafinil and ketamine.
evidence.quote: Results reveal substantial agreement for high-performing models, such as Google AI's Gemini 2.0 Flash, which achieved the highest Cohen's kappa value of 0.82 (SE = 0.052).

evidence.title: A cross-sectional study on ChatGPT's alignment with clinical practice guidelines in musculoskeletal rehabilitation
evidence.outcome: Rater-scored alignment of ChatGPT answers with musculoskeletal rehabilitation clinical practice guidelines
evidence.effect: Mean Likert scores: clarity 4.85, accuracy 4.62, relevance 4.50, completeness 4.20, consistency 3.85; lower agreement and performance in rehabilitation than disease information.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's responses received the highest average score for clarity (4.85), followed by accuracy (4.62), relevance (4.50), and completeness (4.20).

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models GPT-4o, llama 3.1, and qwen 2.5 for cancer genetic variant classification
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM clinical knowledge on variant actionability versus expert annotations
evidence.effect: GPT-4o accuracy 0.7318, Qwen 2.5 0.5731, Llama 3.1 0.4976 in distinguishing clinically relevant variants from VUS; all models tended to overclassify to higher evidence levels.
evidence.quote: All three models showed a tendency to assign variants to higher evidence levels, suggesting a propensity for overclassification.

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of language models in addressing syphilis-related queries
evidence.venue: Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal
evidence.outcome: LLM syphilis answer accuracy versus WHO fact sheets and specialist review
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 4.0 92% and Claude 89% WHO alignment; Perplexity and Llama3 60-70%; specialists found outdated treatment protocols; only 60% of content clinically reliable without edits.
evidence.quote: Specialists identified common errors, such as outdated treatment protocols and incorrect descriptions of transmission pathways.

evidence.title: ChatGPT and Google Gemini are Clinically Inadequate in Providing Recommendations on Management of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Compared to American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence.venue: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy and completeness versus AAOS DDH clinical practice guideline recommendations
evidence.effect: Accurate in 5/9 (ChatGPT-4.0), 6/9 (ChatGPT-3.5), 6/9 (Gemini); incomplete in 7/9, 6/9, 7/9 recommendations; no significant differences between chatbots.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.0, ChatGPT-3.5, and Google Gemini were accurate in 5/9, 6/9, 6/9, supplementary in 8/9, 7/9, 9/9, and incomplete in 7/9, 6/9, 7/9 recommendations, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: questions derived from AAOS CPG recommendations

evidence.title: Subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus internus deep brain stimulation for the treatment of parkinson's disease: An artificial intelligence approach
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with CNS guideline recommendations on STN/GPi DBS
evidence.effect: Concordance was 42.9% ChatGPT 4o and 28.6% each for Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini; over-conclusive responses 42.8-57.1%; insufficient 14.3-28.6%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT 4o showcased 42.9% concordance, with non-concordant responses classified as 14.3% insufficient and 42.8% over-conclusive.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT and DeepSeek in postdural puncture headache management: a comparative study with international consensus guidelines
evidence.outcome: LLM answers' accuracy and completeness versus 2023 PDPH consensus guidelines
evidence.effect: All four models 100% accurate (10/10); incompleteness (omission of critical guideline content) was 80% ChatGPT-4o, 70% DeepSeek-R1, 60% ChatGPT-4o mini and DeepSeek-V3 (p = 0.729).
evidence.quote: Though largely accurate, their responses achieve only 60-80% completeness relative to medical guidelines.

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT's performance in providing treatment recommendations for pediatric diseases
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT pediatric treatment recommendations by disease type, question type, and error category
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 82.2% (95% CI 81.0%-83.4%); common diseases 84.4%; prone to errors in disease definitions, medications, and surgical treatment.
evidence.quote: However, it was prone to errors in disease definitions, medications, and surgical treatment.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Performance of State-of-the-Art Artificial Intelligence Chatbots Based on the WHO Global Guidelines for the Prevention of Surgical Site Infection: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy of recommendations and rationales against WHO SSI prevention guidelines (5-point Likert)
evidence.effect: Recommendation accuracy mean 4.03 (SD 1.09); rationale accuracy 3.74 (SD 0.91) and comprehensiveness 3.85 (SD 0.83), moderate level; harm scores ≥4.
evidence.quote: In contrast, consistency (mean 3.94, SD 0.72), clarity (mean 3.94, SD 0.89), comprehensiveness (mean 3.85, SD 0.83), and accuracy (mean 3.74, SD 0.91) performed at a moderate level.

evidence.title: Battle of the artificial intelligence: a comprehensive comparative analysis of DeepSeek and ChatGPT for urinary incontinence-related questions
evidence.outcome: Guideline adherence of chatbot responses to AUA/SUFU and EAU urinary incontinence guidelines
evidence.effect: Fully compliant responses: DeepSeek 11 (73.33%), ChatGPT-4.0 13 (86.67%), P = 0.651; occasional deviations observed.
evidence.quote: Regarding guideline adherence, DeepSeek had 11 (73.33%) fully compliant responses, while ChatGPT-4.0 had 13 (86.67%), with no significant difference [P = 0.651, Cohen's w = 0.083 (95% CI: 0.021, 0.232)].

evidence.title: Comparing GPT-4o and o1 in Otolaryngology: An Evaluation of Guideline Adherence and Accuracy
evidence.outcome: Guideline-concordant accuracy of LLM answers to otolaryngology questions, graded by blinded otolaryngologists
evidence.effect: o1: 73% correct, 26% partially correct, 1% incorrect (mean 0.86); GPT-4o: 64% correct, 36% partially correct, 0% incorrect (mean 0.82); difference not significant (paired t test P=0.165).

commentary.bottom_line: Six small offline or benchmark studies suggest that testing AI output against current guidelines and scoring differentials for serious conditions can reveal knowledge gaps and error rates that vary by model, topic, and patient group. No study shows that this testing, once adopted, reduces missed diagnoses or contraindications in patient care.

perspectives.view: All six tests are level 4 or 5 designs, mostly vignettes or question sets of 30 to 384 items, and none measured patient outcomes. Findings are inconsistent: guideline accuracy ranged from 80% to 86% in two studies, while antibiotic answers were complete and correct in only 27.5% to 38.1% of special-population cases. Indirectness and imprecision support a very low rating.

In one hazard study, errors of omission made up more than 80% of severe errors, which is the failure this testing targets. A replay of 43 emergency notes found a must-not-miss condition in the top three in 78.0% of cases with one system versus 52.0% for a standalone model. This suggests prioritization scoring can separate safer from less safe configurations.

In a dental trauma chatbot, initial completeness of 53% for primary tooth fractures rose to 100% in most cases after code adjustments. This suggests guideline testing may be most useful as an iterative development loop. Retrieval grounding lowered major guideline deviations from 38.1% to 7.9% in one hazard study, which evaluators could use as a comparator.

Error rates in one test reached 79.2% for kidney disease and 25% for older adults, compared with 11.9% for pregnancy. Evaluation sets that omit such subgroups may overstate accuracy. One test used Chinese-language guidelines. In a Rwanda deployment with community health workers, both models missed important conditions, and no test examined similar settings.

A regulatory discussion paper names differential completeness and prioritization of serious diagnoses as possible device testing, using permissive language. The supplied studies do not show which test design or threshold would satisfy a reviewer. Accuracy moved from 84% to 86% over 30 days in one benchmark, which suggests repeat testing after model updates may be needed.

The physician's most probable diagnosis was omitted in 19.6% of consultations in one real-world symptom tool. Patients who use such tools may not know which conditions were left out. Published guideline and differential test results could help patients and clinicians judge how far to rely on the output.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares deployments that underwent guideline and differential testing with those that did not, and none links test scores to missed diagnoses, contraindication errors, or harm in live care. Evaluators also lack evidence on how often to retest after guideline or model changes.
commentary.underserved_note: One test used non-English questions scored against Chinese guidelines, and one included older adults, where error rates were higher. No test included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations, so health systems serving these groups cannot assume published accuracy figures apply to their patients.
